It is a hands-on product engineering role for someone who can understand the problem, shape the user experience, think through the system design and then build high-quality software.
The role is primarily focused on React, TypeScript and modern user experience development, but the expectation is broader than UI delivery. You will work close to lawyers, knowledge teams, innovation teams and technical stakeholders to understand how AI search, retrieval and agents should fit into real legal workflows.
We are not building another disconnected AI chatbot. We are building trusted AI experiences that sit on top of the firm’s own documents, knowledge, matters, metadata and workflows.
As a Product Engineer, you will help turn complex AI retrieval capability into simple, useful and trusted experiences for lawyers.
# **Why This Role Matters**
AI is changing software engineering. The value of an engineer is no longer only in writing code quickly. AI can now help generate code, tests and components at speed. That makes the human part of engineering more important, not less.
The best engineers are now the ones who understand the system, the user, the constraints and the business problem.
For this team, that means understanding why a lawyer is searching, what they need to trust an answer, what happens if the wrong document is surfaced, how permissions work, how citations should be displayed, and how the experience fits into their daily workflow.
A button is not just a button. A search result is not just a card. An AI answer is not just text on a page.
In legal AI, every interaction has to support trust, explainability, security and adoption.
That is why we need Product Engineers: people who are fluent in engineering, fluent in product thinking, and willing to understand the domain deeply enough to build the right thing.
# **About the Team**
The Search & AI team helps law firms build secure, firm-specific AI capabilities on top of their existing document, knowledge and matter infrastructure.
We work with firms that want to move beyond standalone AI tools and create a trusted AI layer inside their own environment. Our solutions typically connect to systems such as iManage, SharePoint, NetDocuments, Microsoft 365, Azure AI Search, Azure OpenAI and internal knowledge platforms.
The team already has experience delivering AI search and workflow capabilities for a Magic Circle law firm and a global multinational law firm, including natural language search, agents and Azure-based retrieval solutions built in partnership with Microsoft.
As the market shifts from AI adoption to AI ownership, our team is becoming more like a Forward Deployment Engineering function: technical people who work close to strategic clients, understand their workflows, and build real solutions that move from prototype to production.
# **The Role**
You will design and build the product experience layer for legal AI.
That includes search interfaces, AI answer experiences, document previews, citation views, agent workflows, feedback loops, dashboards, admin screens and embedded components for tools lawyers already use.
You will mainly work in React and TypeScript, building polished, enterprise-grade applications that are fast, accessible, secure and suitable for professional legal users.
You will work with AI engineers, retrieval architects, Azure engineers, legal knowledge experts and client stakeholders to turn complex technical capabilities into clear, usable products.
# **What You Will Build**
You may build a natural language search experience that allows lawyers to ask questions across a firm’s knowledge bank and receive grounded answers with citations.
You may create a source preview panel that lets a lawyer inspect the exact document behind an AI answer before relying on it.
You may design an agent workflow where a lawyer can run a research task, review retrieved documents, refine the question, compare outputs and export the result.
You may build dashboards that show search quality, adoption, answer confidence, feedback trends and retrieval performance.
You may create embedded components for SharePoint, Teams, Word, Outlook or a firm intranet, so AI appears inside the workflow rather than as another destination.
The common thread is that you will be building the experience layer that makes AI usable, explainable and trusted.
# **Key Responsibilities**
**Build high-quality React and TypeScript applications**
You will build modern front-end applications using React, TypeScript and strong component design. You will care about performance, accessibility, responsiveness, error handling, loading states, empty states, maintainability and the overall quality of the user experience. You will work with APIs, authentication, permissions, search services, AI responses, document metadata and workflow actions.
**Shape the product, not just the code**
You will help define how legal AI experiences should work. This means challenging unclear requirements, simplifying complex workflows, proposing better interaction patterns and making sure the team is building something users will actually adopt. You will not just wait for a perfect specification. You will help create it.
**Understand the lawyer workflow**
You will work close to legal users and client teams to understand how lawyers search for knowledge, review documents, validate answers and move through their work. The goal is to build AI into workflows lawyers already understand, rather than sending them to another disconnected tool.
**Turn AI retrieval into trusted UX**
You will design interfaces that make retrieval transparent. This includes citations, source previews, metadata, snippets, filters, document cards, confidence signals, feedback mechanisms and audit-friendly interaction patterns. In legal AI, the user needs to understand where an answer came from and why it should be trusted.
**Work across the system**
Although this is mainly a React and TypeScript role, you will need to understand how your UI fits into the wider system. That may include Azure AI Search, Azure OpenAI, retrieval APIs, MCP-style tool access, document processing pipelines, security trimming, Microsoft Graph, SharePoint, iManage or other enterprise systems. You do not need to own every layer, but you should understand how the layers connect.
**Use AI as part of your engineering workflow**
We expect Product Engineers to use AI effectively in their own work. That may include using AI to generate code drafts, test ideas, explore components, accelerate refactoring or support documentation. But the judgement remains yours. AI can help write code. It cannot own the product intent, system consequences or user trust.
# **Required Skills**
You should have strong hands-on experience with React and TypeScript.
You should be comfortable building component-based applications, working with APIs, handling complex state and delivering polished enterprise user interfaces. Experience with Next.js would be useful, but is not essential.
You should understand modern front-end development practices, including authentication flows, role-based permissions, asynchronous data, loading states, error states, accessibility, testing, source control and CI/CD.
Experience with some of the following would be valuable: React Query, Zustand, Redux, Tailwind, Fluent UI, Material UI, Vite, Next.js, Storybook, Playwright, Jest, Azure Static Web Apps, Azure App Service or Microsoft Graph.
You do not need to be a deep AI engineer, but you should be interested in AI product design and willing to learn how retrieval, citations, agents and RAG systems work.
# **Product Engineering Mindset**
The strongest candidates will think beyond tickets.
You should be someone who wants to understand why something is being built, not just how to build it. You should be comfortable working in ambiguity, forming a point of view, testing ideas quickly and improving based on feedback.
You should care about systems. You should want to understand how the UI, API, retrieval layer, permissions model and user workflow fit together.
You should be able to see where a small UI decision could create confusion, risk or unnecessary friction.
You should also care about product quality. Legal users are time-poor and sceptical of poor AI experiences. The interface needs to be clear, reliable and professional.
This is a role for someone who wants to use engineering judgement, product instinct and domain understanding together.
# AI and Search Awareness
You will work around AI search and retrieval systems, so you should be interested in concepts such as retrieval-augmented generation, semantic search, vector search, hybrid search, document chunking, citations, source grounding, prompt workflows and agentic interfaces.
You do not need to build all of this from scratch, but you do need to understand enough to design good user experiences around it.
For example, when an AI answer is shown, the UI should help the lawyer answer practical questions: Where did this answer come from? Can I open the source? Is this the latest version? Which jurisdiction does this relate to? Who authored it? Can I trust this document? What should I do next?
That is product engineering in legal AI.
# **Desirable Experience**
Experience in any of the following would be useful: legal technology, enterprise search, document management systems, knowledge management, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, iManage, NetDocuments, Azure AI Search, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Graph, Power Platform, SaaS products, internal tools, workflow platforms or professional services.
Experience building search interfaces, AI interfaces, dashboards, document review tools, knowledge portals or workflow applications would be particularly relevant.
# **What Success Looks Like**
Success means the team builds AI products that lawyers actually use.
A successful search experience will help a lawyer find the right precedent, legal opinion or knowledge document quickly and confidently.
A successful answer experience will make the source material visible, citeable and easy to inspect.
A successful agent workflow will guide the user through a complex task without hiding important decisions.
A successful product will feel simple on the surface, even though the system underneath is complex.
More broadly, success means helping law firms move from AI experimentation to AI capability they can trust, own and scale.
# **Example Projects**
• A legal knowledge search application over SharePoint or iManage content.
• A React/TypeScript AI answer interface with citations, filters and source previews.
• A document preview panel showing metadata, snippets and highlighted evidence.
• An agent workflow for precedent discovery, matter research or legal opinion search.
• A dashboard showing adoption, answer quality, feedback and retrieval performance.
• An embedded SharePoint or Teams component that brings AI search into an existing lawyer workflow.
• A configuration experience for managing sources, prompts, retrieval settings or access controls.
• A feedback interface that helps improve retrieval quality over time.
# **Ideal Candidate**
The ideal candidate is a strong React TypeScript developer who wants to operate more like a Product Engineer.
You are hands-on, technical and comfortable building production software. But you also want to understand the user, the workflow and the system around the code.
You may come from a product engineering background, SaaS company, enterprise software team, professional services environment or start-up.
Legal technology experience would be helpful, but it is not required.
What matters most is that you can build polished front-end applications, think through product problems, work with APIs, collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and move comfortably from prototype to production.
You should be curious about AI, but grounded enough to know that adoption depends on usability, trust and workflow fit.
# **Why Join This Team?**
Legal AI is entering a new phase.
Law firms do not just want generic AI tools. They want AI experiences that understand their own knowledge, systems, permissions and workflows.
This team sits at the centre of that shift.
You will help build the product experiences that make legal AI real for lawyers: not another disconnected Copilot, but one trusted AI layer embedded into the way they already work.
This is the future of engineering in practice: less time spent simply turning specs into code, and more time spent understanding the problem, shaping the system and building the right product.

## The Opportunity
Fitch Ratings is looking for a builder, a challenger, and a boundary-pusher to lead the engineering organization responsible for all applications and services powering our Corporates, Financial Institutions, and Sovereigns lines of business. This is not a role for someone who optimizes within the status quo — it's a role for someone who questions it, reimagines it, and has the courage and capability to do something about it.
As Senior Director, you will have executive ownership of four engineering teams comprising a couple of dozen engineers. You'll lead a talented, multidisciplinary group tackling some of the most consequential technology challenges in global financial intelligence — maintaining and evolving the systems that analysts and clients depend on today, while simultaneously building the next generation of platforms from a position of real creative freedom and organizational backing.
This is a role for someone who moves fast, experiments boldly, and doesn't wait for permission to try something new. Someone who has broken things in the pursuit of building something better, who sees constraints as invitations to be clever, and who brings an infectious sense of possibility that raises the ambition of everyone around them. If you've spent time deep in machine learning or AI systems — not just using them, but building them — that's not just a bonus, it's the kind of background that makes this opportunity even more compelling. But this role goes far beyond any single discipline: it's about leading a culture of relentless innovation across every dimension of how software gets built and delivered.
---
## We'll Count on You To
**Challenge the conventional and set a bolder technical vision** Own the strategic direction, execution, and engineering culture of four high-performing full-stack engineering teams. But more than managing what exists — interrogate it. Ask the uncomfortable questions about why things are built the way they are, and lead your teams toward answers that are smarter, faster, and more powerful. Set a technical vision that doesn't just improve the current state but genuinely reimagines what's possible for the platforms powering Fitch's most critical analytical work.
**Build, develop, and inspire exceptional people** Lead, mentor, and empower a team of team leads and engineers across a range of technical backgrounds and experience levels. Foster a culture where intellectual curiosity is celebrated, where experimentation is encouraged, and where people feel safe enough to take risks and learn loudly from what doesn't work. Attract and retain engineers who are hungry, inventive, and proud of both the quality of what they ship today and the audacity of what they're building toward.
**Reimagine and modernize critical platforms** Oversee the full lifecycle of the applications and services central to Fitch's Corporates, Financial Institutions, and Sovereigns analytical workflows. Balance the discipline of maintaining production-grade systems with the creative ambition to tear down and rebuild what no longer serves the business well. Be the person in the room who asks "what if we started over?" — and who knows when that's exactly the right call.
**Drive greenfield innovation without apology** Identify and actively pursue opportunities to design and build net-new applications and platforms that replace or leapfrog legacy approaches. Embrace the blank canvas — and bring the rigor of world-class software delivery with you. This is an organization that wants to see bets placed, experiments run, and lessons learned fast. Be the kind of leader who creates that energy and channels it into things that last.
**Push the frontier of AI, ML, and intelligent systems** Go beyond adopting AI tools — define how intelligent systems become structural, load-bearing parts of the platforms your teams own. The Data Science Engine is a new capability under the Head of Analytics. Its specialists embed in priority product initiatives while building methods and tools that other teams and products can reuse. We are developing a unified analytics framework that describes what we analyze, how our capabilities relate, and which decisions they support. Our longer-term ambition is to help clients understand how risk moves through the world by connecting data, research and analytical methods across companies, instruments, industries and geographies.
This role has the same dual remit: help selected initiatives deliver working knowledge graph applications, and establish the models, components and practices that future initiatives can adopt. You will work with data scientists, product teams, analysts, AI teams and the Core groups responsible for shared data and platforms. You will also help align our work with broader Fitch initiatives that connect research and intelligence across businesses.

Starting with a real product problem, you will work with subject experts to model the relevant concepts and relationships, write the code and queries, and put a working solution in users’ hands. You will partner with engineering teams to make useful solutions durable and scalable. The model should be clear enough to extend, and it should evolve as real use cases reveal what is needed.
**Research Content and AI**
* Partner with research and content teams on tagging and enrichment that connects documents, topics, entities, events and analytical capabilities. Help make authored research easier to discover and reuse while preserving its source and context.

## **Your day-to-day**
We’re searching for **product-focused Android engineers** to evolve our native mobile app.You’ll take pride in building polished user experiences, and you’ll balance the need for well-tested resilient code with moving fast and iterating.
You’ll be working on a product that is a part of day to day life for more than 15 million people already, and your work here will shape the way that people interact with their finances.
As an Android Engineer at Monzo you'll work in a small, autonomous product squad alongside iOS Engineers, Backend Engineers, User Researchers, Product Designers, Product Managers, QA Testers, and Data Scientists.
You and your team will be responsible for an overall company goal, rather than building a specific feature - you'll have the opportunity to have impact on both *what* we build, and *how* we build it. Mobile engineers at Monzo work on everything from the personal banking product to customer support tools. We also have a small mobile platform squad dedicated to enabling other engineers to move faster.

You'll report to an engineering manager who will meet with you every 1-2 weeks 1:1. They’re dedicated to helping you grow and develop as an engineer.
### Our Android app
Our app is 100% Kotlin, built using MVVM (Model View ViewModel) and Coordinators, and modularised by product feature.
Around 95% of the codebase is in Compose. We use Coroutines, Retrofit and Moshi for API calls and Dagger for dependency injection. We are currently migrating to Kotlinx Serialisation and Metro. Room is our choice for persistence, and we use repositories for interacting with data.
We use GitHub Pull Requests to do code reviews, and write unit tests for our ViewModels, Coordinators, and any other classes which contain logic. We write tests for all of our Compose screens and snapshot test them with Happo. We also use Espresso to test flows, which are executed via our continuous integration system.
We’ve previously written about building Monzo Chat on Android, which goes into detail on some of these elements.

Software that controls megawatt-scale electric drives doesn't just run in the background — it determines whether a naval vessel manoeuvres safely, whether an industrial process runs efficiently, and whether an energy system performs when it matters most. **The Mission: Why We Exist**
Genomics is a science-led transatlantic TechBio combining large-scale genetic and health data with proprietary analytics to accelerate drug discovery and advance predictive, preventative healthcare. We are united by a single vision to help people live longer healthier lives, using the power of genomics.
Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores - giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time.
### Role Purpose
We're looking for an exceptional Data Scientist with a strong background in human genetics and genomics, and advanced skills in data science, statistics and computational analysis. You might be a great fit for this role if you're a methods-oriented domain specialist within the broad field of genomics with some exposure to software engineering practices and an interest in developing that side of your skillset. The primary purpose of the role is to develop and integrate support for processing, quality control and analysis of new types of data into our production and research software tools.
You'll join a team of experts in human genetics, data science and software engineering, building the platform at the heart of our Life Sciences work – helping us derive new insights into human biology and guide drug development towards safer, more effective targets. How your time splits across data processing workflows, statistical methods and software engineering will reflect your own balance of scientific and computational strengths, with an emphasis on genetics domain expertise and data analysis, including processing and interpreting functional genomics data.
This role can be hired at IC2 (Data Scientist) or IC3 (Senior Data Scientist) level, depending on your experience. At IC3, you'll operate with greater autonomy, hold a broader scientific scope, bring deeper subject-matter expertise, and lead analyses that integrate multiple genomic data sources, working with cross-disciplinary teams to deliver value.
### A Day in the Life
At the heart of this role is the opportunity to expand and improve how we use data and cutting edge methods to identify and validate effective and safe drug targets via deeper understanding of disease mechanisms.
* Identify innovative uses of new types of data for integration into our data and analytics platform. E.g from functional genomics and perturbation screens, molecular profiling and expression atlases, genomic and functional annotations, and curated interaction, pathway and ontology resources.
* Implement production quality code for processing, transforming and quality control of new data types for integration into our larger data model
* Contribute to and implement statistical and machine learning methods to a high standard of robustness, validation and reproducibility.
* Contribute to internal and external presentations and publications arising from our work.
* Keep your knowledge current on innovation and good practice in genomics, functional genomics and statistical genetics.
* At Senior (IC3) level, you'll also lead projects that integrate multiple functional genomics and genetic data sources, coordinating with cross-disciplinary teams to deliver value.
### ### Who You Are
### Essential
* Strong knowledge of human genetics and functional or clinical genomics, and the ability to apply it to research questions.
* Skilled at analysing and learning from large-scale biological datasets, including statistical and machine learning methods.
* Experienced processing and interpreting data from functional genomics, molecular and expression atlases, genomic annotations, and curated pathway and interaction resources, including quality control.
* Competent writing code in Python and/or R for data analysis, with an appreciation of good software development practice.
### It'd be great if you also have
* Comfortable using LLM programming assistants appropriately within a research analysis environment.
* Experienced running tools and workflows in a scalable system, for example Linux based HPC environments or on cloud systems.
* Experience working on a collaborative codebase using version control and CI/CD.
* Experience working in remote, cloud-based environments, e.g. AWS.
* Prior experience working in a team, ideally in an industry setting.
* A PhD or postgraduate degree in genetics, genomics, computational biology or bioinformatics, or statistics and machine learning applied in these fields.

## **About Gigs**
At Gigs, we're building the operating system for mobile services—a platform that lets tech companies embed global connectivity into their products effortlessly.
Just as Stripe lets any business add a payment button in seconds, Gigs empowers platforms to weave in connectivity—bridging the traditional world of telecom with modern tech. From fintechs launching mobile services to HR platforms offering work phone plans, we automate provisioning and remove telecom complexity.
Our team of around 150 people across the US and Europe, backed by nearly $100 million in funding from Ribbit Capital, Google, and Y Combinator. As one of the fastest-growing tech companies, bringing together early-stage engineers, product builders, and business athletes from companies like Stripe, Airbnb, and Shopify. We’re tackling deep technical and regulatory challenges to make connectivity truly seamless.
If you’re driven by curiosity, creativity, and the chance to shape the future of telecom, we’d love to hear from you.
## **Things We Care About**
We are building in a highly complex space and tackling a massive problem. We want people who lean in when things get hard.
* **Speed.** We move and we ship. We set bold deadlines and treat every week like it matters.
* **Ownership.** If you see something broken, fix it. We don't wait for permission.
* **Customer Obsession**. Our customers' product is our product.
* **Ambiguity.** We're building frontier technology in a complex domain. You'll need sound judgement and good instincts to make decisions without complete information.
* **First principles.** We don't ask how things have been done before. We ask why they were done that way at all.
## The Role
GTM Associates at Gigs are the engine of top of funnel growth - and the starting point for a career in commercial leadership. You'll work closely with our GTM Lead to identify, qualify, and develop pipeline for Gigs in the UK & Ireland.
This isn't a role where you execute a handed to you playbook. You'll help build it - and the best people here grow fast because of it. Our GTM org is lean by design. You'll have real visibility with senior operators from day one, and the commercial decisions you make will matter.
For the right person, this is a rare early stage opportunity at a company that has already proven its model in multiple markets and is now executing fast in the UK & Ireland.
**What you will do**
* **You'll go after the accounts that matter most.** You'll work a focused list of must win UK & Ireland accounts - across fintech & banking, retail, travel, utilities and devices - and your job is to get Gigs in the room with them. Depth over volume: a small number of named accounts, pursued brilliantly.
* **You'll grow into deals fast.** You'll start by sourcing and qualifying, and advance on capability, not tenure. Run your accounts well and you'll be leading first conversations within your first few quarters, on a clear path (Shadow → Lead → Own) toward deal ownership.
* **You'll get creative about how we get there.** Warm introductions, conferences and events, content, product hooks - the London fintech circuit is dense, and you'll pick the rooms that matter, get us into them, and turn conversations into pipeline.
* **You'll own inbound for the region.** You'll respond fast, qualify with discipline, and make confident calls on fit.
* **You'll learn the product deeply and make our playbook better.** You'll get to grips with our infrastructure, learn why it matters to each buyer, and feed what you learn back into how we sell.
* **You'll work AI-first.** Research, outreach, account mapping - you'll run our top of funnel tooling stack, use AI as a natural part of how you work, and iterate on what performs.
* **What success looks like:**At 3 months, you know the product and you're running quality first conversations. At 6 months, we're in rooms with must win accounts through paths we wouldn't have found without you. At 12 months, you're leading conversations independently and working live deals alongside the GTM Lead
**What we are looking for**
* **You have a high growth commercial mindset.** You've spent 2-4 years in a commercial, strategy or analytically rigorous role e.g. sales, business development, partnerships, consulting, VC or adjacent - ideally working with founders, operators or senior buyers in UK fintech and tech. You look for the warm path before defaulting to cold. We care more about how you think than where you've worked.
* **You're analytically sharp and structured by default.** You form a hypothesis, test it, and revise. You bring order to ambiguity and your work is reliable enough that senior people build on it.
* **You're an exceptional communicator.** You make complex ideas simple.
* **You're a self-starter who cares about outcomes.** You don't wait for a playbook - you help build one. And you measure yourself on commercial impact, not activity.
* **You're energised by technology.** You love the idea of businesses embedding mobile connectivity into their products and you want to sell the infrastructure that makes it possible.
## Work At Gigs
At Gigs, we value in-person collaboration. We believe the best ideas, decisions, and relationships are built when teams spend meaningful time together, and our culture is designed around that belief. We support flexibility where it makes sense. Some focused work can be done remotely, and not every role or week looks the same. **You should expect regular time in one of our** **hubs**, as well as occasional travel for team workshops, customer meetings, and **Gigs Republic, our bi-annual company off-site**. Our offices are designed to feel like home-inspired workspaces, with plants, thoughtful tools, and small, tight-knit teams that make collaboration feel natural, energizing, and effective.
## What We Offer
At Gigs, we believe in rewarding excellence. We offer competitive compensation and stock options because we see you as a true partner in our growth. We also provide stipends for your home office or work setup, a budget for learning and development to fuel your career, and of course, a free phone and international data plan

# Onboarding and Customer Success Manager
Norwich, England, United Kingdom
### **The Company**
Glassbox's mission is to empower enterprises to shape trusted, frictionless digital experiences.

### The Opportunity
We are seeking a highly organized and customer-centric Onboarding and Customer Success Manager (CSM) to join our team in a dynamic, hybrid role. This position serves as the critical bridge between the sales cycle and long-term customer value. Your primary focus will be owning the initial onboarding phase-acting as a project manager to ensure new customers are successfully implemented, trained, and realizing time-to-value as quickly as possible. Because our account distribution is highly adaptable, the post-onboarding lifecycle will vary. Depending on the customer segment, product tier, and team capacity, you will either formally transition the customer to a dedicated ongoing CSM upon successful deployment, or you will retain the account and manage their long-term success and growth. You must be equally adept at rigorous project management and long-term relationship building.
### What You Will Do?
**Implementation & Onboarding (All Accounts)**
* Project Management: Lead post-sale kickoff meetings, align on customer goals, and develop tailored, time-bound onboarding project plans.
* Platform Implementation: Pair with technical counterparts to guide customers through technical setup, integration configurations, and best practices to ensure a flawless deployment.
* Training & Education: Conduct and schedule comprehensive product training sessions tailored to various user personas (e.g., admins, end-users, executive sponsors) to drive immediate platform adoption.
* Time-to-Value Delivery: Monitor early adoption metrics and proactively address bottlenecks to ensure customers achieve their first defining moment of value within the targeted onboarding window.
**Account Transition & Handoffs**
* Milestone Evaluation: Define and evaluate clear "graduation" criteria to determine when an account has successfully completed onboarding.
* Internal Alignment: Collaborate with Sales, Support, CX, and the broader CS team to determine post-onboarding account ownership.
* Seamless Handoffs: For accounts moving to a different CSM, prepare comprehensive handover documentation detailing the customer's goals, current health, potential risks, and technical setup, facilitating a warm introduction and smooth transition.
**Ongoing Customer Success (For Retained Accounts)**
* Relationship Management: Serve as the trusted advisor and primary point of contact for a designated portfolio of post-onboarding customers.
* Strategic Reviews: Conduct Executive Business Reviews (EBRs) / Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) to demonstrate ROI, align on upcoming business objectives, and introduce relevant new features.
* Retention & Growth: Identify expansion opportunities (upsells/cross-sells) and partner with Sales to execute them.
* Health Monitoring: Continuously monitor customer health scores, proactively identifying churn risks and building robust mitigation strategies.
* Customer Advocacy: Identify successful customers to participate in case studies, webinars, and referral programs.

* Customer Success Experience: 3+ years of experience in Customer Success, Implementation, or B2B SaaS Account Management.

* Adaptability: Comfort operating in a flexible environment where account ownership and daily priorities can shift based on business needs.
* BSFI: Experience in the BFSI field is a plus.

## Fractional CISO (Contract / Project Based)
**Location:** Remote **Type:** Contracted **Level:** Experienced
### Engagement Overview
This engagement is strictly deliverable-focused. You will not be integrating into day-to-day operations or managing staff. Instead, you will provide senior, independent judgment and set the overarching security strategy, which will be executed by the internal IT & Systems Manager. This deliberate separation between control definition and operational execution ensures the objective assurance required by regulated client base.
### Key Deliverables & Outcomes
You will maintain full autonomy over how these outcomes are achieved as an external advisor, partnering with the Head of Engineering (acting SIRO) as your primary internal contact.
* **Security Strategy & Roadmap:** Define a clear, costed security strategy and sequenced improvement roadmap tailored to the evolving estate, threat landscape, and risk appetite.
* **Risk & Assurance Stewardship:** Architect a security-specific risk register and conduct regular, independent reviews of the control environment operated by the internal IT team.
* **Board Reporting:** Deliver periodic board-level reporting on organisational risk.
* **Certification Direction:** Deliver a formal, evidence-based recommendation on whether to pursue ISO 27001 or maintain Cyber Essentials Plus with a documented ISMS.
* **Incident Framework:** Design an incident response framework, testing plans, escalation pathways, and playbooks. (Note: Hands-on involvement in a live serious incident will be treated as a separate, ad-hoc call-off engagement).
* **Client Assurance & Board Reporting:** Mature the existing reusable security assurance evidence library for complex client due-diligence.
### Operational Boundaries
To ensure unambiguous B2B boundaries and maintain focus on strategic deliverables, the following operational execution remains firmly with Cambridge Spark:
* **Execution & First Response:** Hands-on operations (patching, endpoint hardening, configuration) and incident first-response are owned by the internal IT & Systems Manager.
* **Routine Questionnaires:** Standard client security questionnaires will be completed by the internal team against the standards and evidence library you define.
* **Accountability & Compliance:** Final accountability sits with the SIRO. Data protection (DPO duties) and AI compliance (e.g., EU AI Act classification) sit with internal compliance owners, whom you will advise on security overlaps.
### Engagement Model & Commercials
This is a phased, fractional engagement designed around project deliverables rather than a fixed weekly schedule. The cadence will naturally follow the required outputs:
* **Setup Phase (~First 3 months):** Estimated at 1.5 days per week (approx. 17–19 days total) to deliver the initial risk assessment, strategy, certification recommendation, and incident playbooks.
* **Transition Phase (Months 4–6):** Tapering to approximately 2 days per month as the roadmap moves into internal execution and the first independent assurance reviews commence.
* **Steady State (Month 6 onwards):** A lightweight retainer of 1–2 days per month for ongoing independent assurance, board reporting, and advisory services.
## About the Company
Cambridge Spark is an education technology company that enables corporate and government organisations to achieve their business goals by educating their workforce with critical data transformation skills to succeed in the AI era. The company currently holds Cyber Essentials Plus certification.

About the role
# The Capacity Planning & Forecasting Lead is accountable for leading the development, ownership and continuous improvement of robust, data-driven capacity plans and demand forecasts across Helpdesk and Operations. This role owns the production of accurate short, medium and long-term forecasts, the integrity of capacity models, and the delivery of insight that enables confident operational, financial and commercial decision-making. Working under the direction of the Senior Manager – Enterprise Capacity Planning & Insights, the Lead ensures supply and demand are aligned through disciplined planning, rigorous analysis, proactive stakeholder engagement and clear governance of planning assumptions. This role is critical in enabling efficient and effective operations, ensuring resource plans support service performance, financial discipline, cost efficiency and wider commercial objectives.
**Key Responsibilities**
**1. Capacity Planning & Resource Modelling**
* Lead the design, ownership and maintenance of operational capacity plans across Helpdesk & Operations, ensuring plans are robust, governed and aligned to demand, service commitments and business priorities.
* Own the balance between service performance, resource availability, cost efficiency and commercial outcomes, ensuring capacity recommendations are evidence-based and financially responsible.
* Set out clear hiring, redeployment and resource recommendations across operational roles, influencing senior stakeholders through clear rationale, scenario modelling and commercial impact assessment.
* Track actual versus planned recruitment, attrition, shrinkage and productivity assumptions, providing early warning of risks to service, cost or delivery outcomes.
* Continuously refine planning assumptions, productivity inputs and model design to improve accuracy, resilience and confidence in workforce plans.
**2. Demand Forecasting & Analytics**
* Own and produce short, medium and long-term demand forecasts using appropriate statistical techniques, operational insight and workforce planning methodologies.
* Lead forecast accuracy management through structured validation, back-testing, variance tracking and continuous model refinement.
* Lead detailed planned versus actual analysis, identifying material variances, underlying drivers and the financial or operational implications of changes in demand.
* Challenge and govern forecasting assumptions, using root cause analysis to improve precision, explain movements and support credible decision-making.
* Translate demand trends, risks and opportunities into clear recommendations for operational leaders, Finance, Change and senior stakeholders.
* Design, own and communicate recovery plans when service levels, demand, capacity or cost performance move outside agreed expectations.
**3. Workforce Management & Planning**
* Lead the effective use of Workforce Management systems, ensuring planning data, assumptions and outputs are accurate, consistent and trusted by operational teams.
* Proactively identify emerging trends, operational pressures or unforeseen risks, leading timely interventions to protect service, cost and colleague capacity outcomes.
* Drive continuous improvement in WFM tools, planning processes and governance, ensuring outputs are scalable, repeatable and aligned to enterprise planning standards.
* Identify efficiency opportunities, operational leakage and areas for optimisation, quantifying the service, cost and commercial benefit of proposed actions.
* Lead cross-functional planning conversations with Operations, Finance, Change and senior stakeholders, ensuring plans are understood, challenged appropriately and translated into action.
**4. Financial Planning & Forecasting**
* Lead workforce input into budget planning, reforecasting and quarterly financial forecasts for Helpdesk & Operations, ensuring assumptions are transparent, evidence-based and operationally credible.
* Own the alignment between capacity plans, demand forecasts, service commitments and financial targets, escalating risks and trade-offs with clear recommendations.
* Deliver cost optimisation through improved resource utilisation, productivity insight, scenario modelling and clear identification of opportunities to improve commercial outcomes.
**5. Change Impact & Planning Governance**
* Lead capacity and demand impact assessments for business initiatives affecting Operations and Helpdesk, ensuring service, cost, FTE and commercial implications are clearly understood.
* Own the incorporation of product, process, regulatory, volume and operating model changes into forecasts and capacity plans, ensuring assumptions are documented and aligned across functions.
* Apply and strengthen capacity planning governance, ensuring planning decisions are traceable, assumptions are clear and senior stakeholders have confidence in the outputs.
* Lead best-practice adoption across planning processes, using lessons learned, performance data and stakeholder feedback to improve future planning cycles.
**Key Accountabilities**
* Ownership, accuracy and reliability of demand forecasts, capacity plans and planning assumptions.
* Credibility of planning outputs with Heads of Operations, Helpdesk, Finance and Change stakeholders.
* Effectiveness of variance analysis, root cause identification and corrective action planning.
* Measurable improvement in forecast accuracy, model quality and planning confidence over time.
* Alignment of capacity with service level commitments, financial targets and commercial priorities.
* Contribution to operational efficiency, cost optimisation and benefit realisation.
* Responsiveness to emerging demand trends, operational risks and changes in business priorities.
* Ownership of recovery plans when service, cost, capacity or forecast accuracy moves outside agreed business appetite.
**Skills & Experience Required**
**Essential**
* Proven experience leading capacity planning, demand forecasting or workforce planning activity within a contact centre, operations or enterprise planning environment.
* Strong understanding of workforce management and staffing methodologies.
* Strong track record of owning forecast accuracy, capacity modelling and planning governance across short, medium and long-term horizons.
* Advanced Excel skills and experience with statistical modelling techniques.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving capability with high attention to detail.
* Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders by translating complex datasets into clear insight, options, risks and commercially grounded recommendations.
* Proactive, organised, and self-sufficient working style.
**Desirable**

## About Hesta
Hesta is setting a new benchmark in women's health, delivering exceptional, evidence-based clinical care at every life stage, starting with pregnancy and the two years after birth. We combine compassionate care with technology built at the forefront of AI-native healthcare.
75 million years of women's lives are lost every year to poor health or early death. Not because these conditions are rare, but because almost no one has been paid to look into them properly. We're changing that.
We raised our pre-seed round last year, alongside grant funding to launch Hesta Labs. Within months of founding we operationalised a CQC-registered multidisciplinary healthcare service, have already cared for hundreds of women, and been featured in The Times.
Cofounders:
* Dr Sujitha Selvarajah: NHS OBGYN doctor with a global public health background. Has worked with the WHO and The Lancet, and is an ex-researcher at Oxford and UCL.
* Amanda Cupples: ex-Managing Director, Airbnb UK, Northern Europe and MEA; ex-COO, Babylon; ex-McKinsey and Deluxe.
Supported by world-leading clinical, product and technology advisors, and backed by investors including Eka, Blue Lion, Ascension and others.
**What women who've used Hesta are saying:**
"Surpassed any expectations. Highly recommend."
"I have never felt this listened to or heard by a GP before. I felt very empowered and supported."
**What clinicians, including GPs, are saying:**
"This is so good. Women won't even need to see the GP with this. This is even better than most GPs."
We're early-stage: genuine ownership, genuine impact, and the chance to build something that doesn't exist yet, that changes millions of lives.
## About Hesta Labs
Hesta Labs is Hesta's research and development arm, backed by £1.4m in grant funding.
In health, there are only two categories of things: what we know, and what we don't. The second category in women’s health is a chasm. Women weren't required to be included in clinical trials until the early 1990s, and even now, only a sliver of health research funding goes towards conditions that affect women specifically..
Hesta's core service proves that operationalising the known changes lives today. But we've come to believe something else just as firmly: you cannot operationalise your way out of a gap this size. If the evidence was never built, the data never captured, the solutions never tested, somebody has to go and build it. That's what Labs is for.
We tested that belief before we committed to it. Using an Innovate UK grant, we ran a feasibility study with Modality Partnership, delivering care to hundreds of women across East Surrey, Yorkshire and Birmingham, and asked three questions: is this clinically valuable, is this technically possible, and do women actually love it? We found yes, yes and yes.
Labs runs on three principles: invest in the unknown, play and experiment with rigour, and seek out the data that actually changes care. Today that means our current feasibility study under the 2025 Femtech & AI programme, and our newly awarded Innovate UK Biomedical Catalyst grant, over £1.4m, taking Hesta from a validated feasibility study to a scalable repeatable solution.
## The role
We're hiring a Founding Associate for Hesta Labs.
You have to be hungry. Hungry for this role, hungry to make a difference, hungry to get things done and bring people with you.
We want a generalist who can move fluidly between clinical, technical, regulatory and commercial workstreams, who turns ambiguity into a plan without waiting to be told how.
You'll work directly with founders, clinicians and technical team members, and across a high-calibre network of partners: NHS Trusts, academic institutions, regulatory advisors and specialist clinicians. Your job is to turn the oxymoron of ambitiguity and clear vision into a delivered, regulator-ready product and evidence base, in the most time- and cost-efficient way possible.

* Lead our Innovate UK Biomedical Catalyst programme (£1.4m, 18 months) end to end, owning milestones, dependencies and outputs.
* Solve whatever's in the way: designing a communication sequence, onboarding a trial site, sorting a data flow, working out what a regulatory requirement means for us in practice.
* Coordinate across multiple workstreams (clinical, technical, regulatory, commercial), managing interdependencies and critical paths.
* Stay on top of the numbers: own financial planning and data-driven project metrics.
* Steer the path from product and research findings to a regulated, Software as a Medical Device (SaMD).
* Define the plan alongside our Co-Founders, flag risks early, and handle reporting and financial management, including formal change requests where scope or budget shifts.
* Drive alignment and action across internal teams, NHS partners, academic collaborators and external suppliers.
* Feed what we're learning back into product and go-to-market decisions.
* Contribute to future strategy and shaping Hesta's R&D roadmap.
## What you'll bring

Tell us about a time you got something done that mattered, where nobody gave you permission to start it, and nobody had to push you to finish it. What was it, why did you do it, and what happened?

# Systems and Customer Journey Manager
## Own the systems and customer journeys behind our installer businesses, improving CRM, processes and technology to deliver better customer experiences.
**Salary:** Up to £65,000 depending on experience **Role type:** Permanent, 5 days per week, Monday to Friday **Location:** Hybrid, based at our London office, with occasional travel to our installer businesses **Reporting to:** Sales Operations Director (Installs) or Operations Director (Installs) **Direct Reports:** None
## **About Hometree**
Join Hometree at the most exciting moment in our story. Founded in 2015, we've become one of the fastest-growing challengers in the UK home services market, spanning home cover that protects the essential systems in the home, renewable installations like solar, batteries and heat pumps, and the financing that makes them affordable. Together, we help homeowners look after their homes and move to greener, lower-carbon living.
We're now going through the biggest step change in our history. By acquiring OVO Energy's Home Services division, including the trusted CORGI HomePlan and HomeHeat brands, we're becoming one of the UK's leading home services groups, with fresh investment to fuel our next phase of growth. It's a genuine inflection point, and we're looking for people who want to help us build what comes next.
### **Key Achievements**
🏆 UK's third-largest home cover provider: our latest acquisition makes us the third-largest provider of home cover in the UK.
🏆 7 Acquisitions - We've expanded our operations by acquiring 6 key companies across financing (Hometree Finance, formerly Bewarm), Home Cover (Your Repair) and energy services (Geowarmth, The Little Green Energy Company, IMS and GreenGen). And we have most recently announced the acquisition of OVO Home Services and CORGI Homeplan (subject to FCA approval).
🏆 500k Homes Covered - We cover over 500 thousand homes across the UK.
🏆 550+ Employees - We have over 550 passionate employees transforming the industry across the Group, one home at a time.
## **The Role**
You'll own how our systems and processes work for the customer, across our renewables and gas boiler installer businesses: heat pumps, solar, batteries and boiler installs.
You decide what good looks like: how the customer journey should flow, how our CRM and customer communications should work, and where the systems portfolio needs to change so each business can grow. That means getting into the detail of how things work today, finding where we're letting customers down, and building the fix.
Sometimes the fix is new software, not a tweak to what we've got. Where there's a real gap, you'll lead the search: work out what we need, scan the market, and build the case to buy. Once we've chosen, you'll see it through to delivery too, working with Technology, the vendor and the teams who'll use it day to day. You won't write the code, but you'll make sure it lands.
AI is part of this as well. You'll find where it could improve the customer journey, test what looks promising, and bring what works into everyday use. You don't need to have done this before. You do need to be up for it.
You'll usually have more than one of these live at once, pulling in different directions across different businesses. Being methodical matters: work to a plan, keep it on track, and build a clear framework, with your manager's support, for what gets priority when everything feels urgent.
There's a natural link to Home Cover too, particularly insurance and maintenance cross-sell. That's a collaboration, not a responsibility: you'll work with the Home Cover team to align on those journeys and maximise sales both ways.
You'll report to our Sales Operations Director (Installs) or Operations Director (Installs), with a dotted line to our CTO or Head of Product. * **Customer Journey:** Redesign the customer journey from first enquiry through to installation and aftercare, working closely with Sales, Operations and Marketing so everyone's pulling in the same direction.
* **CRM & Communications:** Own the CRM roadmap and customer communications approach for our installer businesses, understanding what each one genuinely needs.
* **Cross-Sell Journeys:** Work with our Home Cover business to align insurance and maintenance cross-sell journeys with installer customers, while creating installation opportunities from Home Cover journeys.
* **Prioritisation:** Build and maintain a framework for prioritising competing work across the systems and customer journey portfolio, agreeing where to focus when priorities conflict.
* **Data & Testing:** Dig into the data to understand what's happening, form hypotheses about what would improve things, and test them before recommending a wider rollout.
* **System Selection:** Lead the search for new systems or software where there's a genuine gap, from scoping requirements and evaluating the market to making the investment case.
* **Implementation:** Help see chosen solutions through to delivery, working with Technology, vendors and the teams using them day to day to get them properly live.
* **AI & Innovation:** Explore, test and help deploy AI within our customer journeys and systems, identifying where it can genuinely improve things for the customer or business.
* **Product & Technology:** Work with the CTO or Head of Product and their teams to turn business needs into solutions they can build, staying involved to ensure the end result works for the customer.
* **Stakeholder Management:** Build strong working relationships across Commercial, Operations, Sales, Marketing, Finance and Technology, at Group level and within each installer business.

Performance incentives and overtime provide the opportunity to achieve higher on-target earnings. **Job Type:** Full-time
## **Join One of the South West’s Leading Renewable Heating Teams**
GreenGenUK is continuing to expand across Devon and Cornwall, and we are looking for an experienced Air Source Heat Pump Service Engineer to join our growing service and maintenance team.
Established in 2011, GreenGenUK has become one of the South West’s leading renewable-energy installers and is proud to be part of the Hometree Group. With more than 50 directly employed team members, a substantial installed customer base and continued investment in our people, there has never been a better time to join us.
We install and maintain hundreds of renewable-heating systems each year and now support more than 1,000 heat pump customers. Our reputation has been built on quality workmanship, strong technical knowledge and excellent customer service.
This is a new, full-time position created as our service and maintenance workload continues to grow.
## **Why Join GreenGenUK?**
✔ South West Renewable Heating Installer of the Year 2025 ✔ Established renewable-energy business with over 50 employees **✔** Part of the Hometree Group ✔ Large and growing heat pump customer base ✔ Strong pipeline of planned service and maintenance work ✔ Company van and paid travel time ✔ Private medical insurance ✔ Performance incentives and overtime opportunities ✔ Working-away opportunities with enhanced rates ✔ Manufacturer training and support for individual systems ✔ Support from an experienced in-house technical team ✔ Long-term job security within a growing sector
## **The Role**
You will carry out planned servicing, fault diagnosis, repairs and performance optimisation on domestic air source heat pump systems throughout Devon and Cornwall.
This is primarily a service and maintenance role. You will need to understand and assess the complete heating system rather than considering the heat pump in isolation. This includes the heat pump, heating controls, hot-water cylinder, pumps, valves, emitters, electrical components and system hydraulics.
**Your work will include:**
* Planned annual servicing of air source heat pump systems
* Attending breakdowns and investigating reported faults
* Mechanical, hydraulic, electrical and controls-based fault finding
* Repairing or replacing defective system components
* Diagnosing poor performance, high energy consumption or comfort issues
* Checking and optimising weather compensation and heating curves
* Reviewing flow temperatures, system pressures, flow rates and temperature differentials
* Inspecting cylinders, pumps, valves, filters, expansion vessels and heating controls
* Completing commissioning checks following installations or remedial works
* Carrying out warranty inspections and manufacturer-authorised remedial work
* Identifying additional repairs and providing clear information for quotations
* Liaising with manufacturers, technical support and our internal operations team
* Explaining system operation clearly to customers
* Providing customers with practical advice on using their system efficiently
* Completing electronic job sheets, photographs, test results and service records
* Maintaining suitable van stock, tools and test equipment
* Supporting installation teams with technical fault finding when required
You will work on systems from manufacturers including Mitsubishi Electric, Vaillant, Samsung and other established heat pump brands.
You do not need previous experience with every system we work on. GreenGenUK will provide manufacturer training and ongoing technical support for individual products and systems.
The role includes paid travel throughout The South West.
## **What We’re Looking For**
We are looking for an experienced and methodical heating engineer who enjoys fault finding and takes pride in resolving problems properly.
You should be confident working independently in customers’ homes while knowing when to seek assistance from manufacturers or GreenGenUK’s wider technical team.
**The successful candidate should have:**
* Practical experience servicing, commissioning or repairing air source heat pumps
* NVQ Level 2 plumbing and heating qualification as a minimum, with Level 3 preferred
* G3 Unvented Hot Water qualification
* Strong knowledge of domestic wet central-heating and hot-water systems
* Good electrical and controls-based fault-finding ability
* An understanding of system balancing, flow rates and weather compensation
* The ability to interpret technical manuals, wiring diagrams and system schematics
* A logical and methodical approach to diagnosing faults
* Strong customer-facing and communication skills
* The ability to explain technical issues in straightforward language
* Confidence using a mobile phone or tablet to complete service records
* The ability to work independently and manage a field-based workload
* A professional attitude and commitment to high-quality workmanship
* A full UK driving licence
## **Desirable Experience**
**The following would be advantageous, although manufacturer and product-specific training will be provided:**
* Mitsubishi Ecodan experience or manufacturer training
* Vaillant aroTHERM experience or manufacturer training
* Samsung heat pump experience or manufacturer training
* Experience working with R290 heat pump systems
* A recognised heat pump installation or service qualification
* Electrical qualifications or formal electrical fault-finding training
* Water Regulations qualification
* F-Gas and/or hydrocarbon refrigerant training
* Experience with underfloor heating and multi-zone heating controls
* Familiarity with MCS standards and renewable-heating commissioning documents
## **What We Offer**
* £35,000–£45,000 salary equivalent, depending on experience
* Performance-related incentives offering the opportunity to earn more
* 40-hour working week
* Paid travel time
* Overtime opportunities
* Enhanced rates for working away
* Company van
* Company pension scheme
* Private medical insurance
* 28 days’ holiday including bank holidays
* Company workwear and PPE
* Tools and test equipment
* Manufacturer training and ongoing support for individual systems
* Support from an experienced operations and technical team
## **Equal Opportunity Employer**
At GreenGenUK, we are committed to creating an inclusive and representative working environment. We know that different experiences, perspectives and backgrounds create a better workplace and a stronger business.
We provide equal opportunities throughout our recruitment process and working environment. Employment decisions are based on experience, skills and suitability for the role.
## **Ready for a New Challenge?**
If you are an experienced engineer who enjoys fault finding, takes pride in delivering excellent customer service and wants to develop within the renewable-heating sector, we would love to hear from you.

Humanis builds symbolic world-models at scale for inference-time safety. We'll provide you with what you need to get up to speed on each industry we're working on. You'll just have to pick it up fast to be able to efficiently interface with customers.

* Own customer follow-up after the initial founder meeting and run meetings throughout the pilot process.
* Scope assessments, pilots, and deployment plans with customers.
* Coordinate technical, security, legal, procurement, and data requests, keeping multiple enterprise opportunities moving in parallel.

Humanoid is seeking a Head of Government Relations to lead the company's engagement with governments, regulators, and industry bodies across its principal markets.
The role reports directly to the Chief Legal Officer and carries a global remit spanning government relations, public affairs, and policy. The United Kingdom is the company's primary market and the United States its fastest-growing second, alongside Canada, Germany, and the European institutions in Brussels.
The remit extends beyond engagement to the development of the company's policy positions, in close alignment with Legal, Finance, and commercial leadership. Three priorities define the role. The first is to establish a regulatory path for the technology, working with governments, regulators, standards bodies, and industry associations so that bipedal platforms, and not solely wheeled systems, can be deployed safely and at scale. * Represent Humanoid before policymakers, officials, and industry bodies, and at public forums and conferences.
* Monitor political and regulatory developments across the United Kingdom, the European Union, and the United States, and advise leadership on their implications for the business.

* A sound working understanding of the United States political environment, and of European Union institutions and policymaking.

* A master's degree or PhD.
* Direct experience in Parliament or government, whether working with or for Members of Parliament, in a ministerial office, or with secretaries and under-secretaries in the executive branch.

* A genuine interest in emerging technologies and the future of robotics.

## Research Software Engineer Job - MDAnalysis software maintainer
#### Kings College London, London, United Kingdom Application deadline: 27 Sep 2026
MDAnalysis is seeking a Research Software Engineer (RSE) to provide dedicated maintenance and development capacity for the MDAnalysis library. This post is funded part-time, 80% FTE by a Software Sustainability Institute Research Software Maintenance Fund (RSMF) grant. The role offers a unique opportunity to have a direct impact on open-source software used by thousands of researchers worldwide across drug discovery, materials science and biophysics.
**Job Description**
The RSE will work across the MDAnalysis codebase on release management, reducing technical debt and maintain interoperability with all major molecular simulation engines. Key deliverables include: maintaining the core library, User Guide and associated ecosystem, implementing support for new trajectory file formats (BCIF/MMCIF, Desmond), modernising the test suite, auditing and documenting CI/CD pipelines and supporting the MDAKits package ecosystem. The RSE will also improve the MDAnalysis UserGuide and tutorial infrastructure and review community pull requests to reduce review cycle times and improve contributor retention.
The post holder will be affiliated to King's College London and work closely with the PI (Dr Micaela Matta), the MDAnalysis Community Manager, and will be supported by a globally distributed team of Core Developers. Day-to-day communication across the team takes place via GitHub, Discord, and regular hybrid meetings.
This is a part-time post (28 hours per week, 0.8 FTE), and you will be offered a fixed term contract for 12 months at Grade 6/35 of King's Single Salary Scale, equivalent to 5-years post-PhD.
Interested candidates are welcome to contact micaela.matta@kcl.ac.uk to discuss the role.
**Essential criteria**
1. PhD qualified in a relevant subject area (e.g. computational chemistry, computational physics, computational materials science, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related discipline), or equivalent professional experience in research software engineering
2. Strong proficiency in Python, including experience with NumPy, SciPy, and the scientific Python ecosystem
3. Demonstrable experience with software engineering best practices: version control (Git/GitHub), continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD), and automated testing
4. Demonstrable experience with managing or contributing to open-source software projects, including code review, issue triage, and release management
5. Ability to write clear technical documentation for both users and developers
6. Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively within a distributed, international team
**Desirable criteria**
1. Demonstrable experience with molecular dynamics simulations or computational chemistry/physics software; knowledge of molecular file formats (PDB, mmCIF, GRO, XTC, DCD, etc.) and simulation engines (GROMACS, AMBER, NAMD, LAMMPS, OpenMM)
2. Familiarity with the MDAnalysis library or similar scientific analysis frameworks (e.g. MDTraj, GROMACS tools, VMD)
3. Demonstrable experience with packaging and distribution of Python software (PyPI, conda-forge)
4. Demonstrable experience with maintaining open-source software projects
5. Experience contributing to or mentoring within open-source communities (e.g. Google Summer of Code)
**How to Apply**
Application link: https://bit.ly/4yzp191
Deadline: September 27
Candidates should submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement detailing how they meet the essential and, where possible, desired criteria listed in the job description.

As a CPM Line Manager, you will provide dedicated line management, leadership, coaching, and functional oversight to an assigned team of Clinical Project Managers within the cFSP model.
Your responsibilities will include:
* Conducting regular 1:1 meetings with direct reports, providing coaching, performance feedback, career development support, and oversight of project responsibilities.
* Setting clear performance expectations and objectives and supporting ongoing performance management.
* Coaching and mentoring team members to support their professional growth, leadership development, and longer-term career progression.

* Reviewing resource allocation and workload across the CPM team and partnering with leadership on capacity planning, succession planning, and backfill activities.

* Partnering with functional leadership, client stakeholders, and operational teams to support effective resource management and clear ways of working.

This is a hands-on security engineering role for people who are deep in cybersecurity and serious about AI. You will secure the AI systems we are building — AI-enabled applications, models, agents, and the platforms beneath them, across their full lifecycle — acting as a trusted advisor who helps define and evolve the firm’s AI security standards, patterns, and guardrails. The objective is not to create additional process, but to ensure our existing security capabilities evolve alongside AI adoption and remain effective at enterprise scale.
Janus Henderson is undertaking a firm-wide AI transformation to become the most technologically sophisticated asset manager in the industry. Our AI capability sits in a single centralised function under the Head of AI, and AI Technology builds and runs it. This role sits in Information Security and reports to the Head of Security Engineering, while your day-to-day work is directed by AI Technology and prioritised against their roadmap. You will secure Nexus, our agentic workspace where employees and citizen developers build and run AI applications, agents, and shared skills; Accio, our centralised MCP server, which consumes other MCP servers and presents enterprise datasets through one governed interface; the AI model gateway and its routes to external model providers; and our Copilot services. Accio and Nexus matter most: both propagate permissions and data on a user’s or an agent’s behalf, so their trust boundaries have to hold when a request crosses several hops. Throughout, you will balance effective risk management against the velocity needed to deliver AI solutions that drive business value and growth.
A secondary focus of the role is partnering with the wider Security function to identify opportunities to leverage AI and automation to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and risk reduction across security operations, engineering, assurance, and governance — so that the controls you design are enforced and evidenced automatically rather than through review meetings.

* Security is designed into AI systems rather than appended. Engineers reach for an approved pattern instead of asking for a bespoke review.
* The controls you define are implemented as code and secure defaults by AI Engineering and AI Platforms, and you can show they are operating.
* AI-specific attacks are anticipated and tested for, and you can demonstrate what the firm is and is not exposed to.
* New models, tools, and Copilot features reach a security decision quickly through a repeatable risk-based path, and when an AI incident happens the lesson lands in a platform default rather than a report.
* Risk reduction and control effectiveness are evidenced through agreed KPIs, KRIs, and reporting rather than asserted.

**Secure the AI estate by design**
* Act as security design authority for AI systems, leading threat modelling, architecture review, and risk assessment for agentic applications, the model gateway, Accio, Nexus, and any novel or high-risk AI initiative, applying STRIDE, PASTA, MITRE ATT&CK, and MITRE ATLAS as appropriate.
* Define and evolve AI security standards, guardrails, governance controls, and secure-by-design patterns aligned with enterprise requirements and the firm’s risk appetite — co-designed with the Principal AI Architect as reusable, implementable guardrails, and implemented as code and secure defaults by AI Engineering and AI Platforms, working with the AI Governance Implementation Lead, who owns how they land on the platform.
* Design identity, entitlement, and secrets patterns for non-human identities — agents, tools, MCP servers, connectors, and service principals — with the Senior AI Platform Engineer and enterprise IAM, covering scoped permissions, credential lifetime, rotation, and least privilege across multi-hop requests.
* Set the trust boundaries and data-egress controls for the AI estate, including what may reach external model providers, and work with data protection owners on classification, DLP enforcement, privacy, and data governance obligations.
**Test, detect, and respond**
* Run adversarial testing and AI red teaming against models, prompts, agents, and tool chains, covering prompt injection and indirect injection, model manipulation and hijacking, excessive agency, function-call abuse, data leakage from LLM outputs, and privilege escalation between agents.
* Build detections, security analytics, and telemetry for AI-specific abuse — anomalous tool invocation, credential misuse by agents, unusual data access, and exfiltration through model responses — and integrate them into the firm’s monitoring estate.
* Support security incident response for AI systems: triage, containment, forensics across prompts, tool calls, and agent decisions, and root cause, feeding each lesson back into platform defaults and evaluation suites.
* Own security testing in the AI delivery lifecycle, including static analysis, dependency and container scanning, secrets detection, and security gates in CI/CD, so issues surface before release.
**Assure AI adoption and third-party risk**
* Co-own the risk-based security gate for onboarding new AI products, model providers, versions, and platform features with the Senior AI Platform Engineer and the AI Governance Implementation Lead, conducting security due diligence and risk assessment of AI vendors, platforms, and models — provenance, open-source components, tenancy and data-use terms, security advisories — and testing platform updates before rollout.

As agents get better at searching for themselves, what is the durable value of a managed retrieval layer? We need someone with an opinionated answer to own JetBrains Context as a product – defining what it is for, who it is for, how we measure success, and where it goes next.

Build and maintain a deep working understanding of chunking, embeddings, index freshness, retrieval, reranking, and agent-facing surfaces.
Define and defend an opinionated vision for the product's evolution, including explicit target audiences, use cases, and key success metrics.
Translate product strategy into actionable problem statements, priorities, plans, and milestones with an explicit definition of “done”.
Communicate product direction clearly to engineering, leadership, cross-functional stakeholders, customers, and prospects.
Analyze competing context and code-search products through direct use to establish clear differentiators and identify gaps.
Define core operational and product metrics – index freshness, retrieval quality, agent task outcomes, adoption, retention, and unit economics – to guide decision-making.
Represent the product externally by sharing roadmaps, publishing updates, speaking to developer audiences, and gathering community feedback.
Partner with ML teams on model evaluation and platform teams on service scale, reliability, and cost.
What you’ll bring
A well-argued point of view on where AI-first development is going and what agents genuinely need from a context layer.
Comfort with technical depth across embeddings, retrieval quality, sub-agents, tool-calling, indexing costs, and API design.
The habit of using the product you build daily alongside competitors' tools.
Communication that adapts to different audiences, from staff engineers and enterprise architects to conference attendees.
A data-informed approach that combines telemetry, evaluation results, customer conversations, and market signals.
Comfort with ambiguity and a preference for defining a new category over copying an existing one.
What you’ll need
Proven experience owning a complex developer, platform, or infrastructure product end to end, including strategy and roadmap.
Hands-on familiarity with modern AI coding tools and agent workflows.
The technical capability to work directly with engineering on retrieval behavior, APIs, data models, and integration surfaces.
The ability to define metrics for quality-sensitive products and build evaluation habits that maintain product standards.
Experience communicating a product externally through written content, talks, or community engagement.
Practical experience with search, retrieval, RAG, developer search, or static analysis at scale is a plus.
What success looks like
Within your first months, you'll form and share a clear thesis for what JetBrains Context is and is not – one the engineering team recognizes as theirs and leadership can invest in. You'll establish a metrics story that distinguishes real retrieval quality from vanity usage, a roadmap with clear trade-offs, and a documented evaluation of serious competitors.
Longer term, success means JetBrains Context becomes a deliberate choice for developers and organizations, agents get measurably better answers because it exists, enterprises adopt it for its governance and scale, and the market clearly understands its unique value because you've communicated it effectively.
