## Role Overview:
We are seeking a Senior Director to lead our Enterprise Reporting and Analytics Engineering organization, a team of analytics engineers, report developers, visualization specialists, and people leaders. This organization focuses on the last mile of the enterprise data supply chain: the semantic models, curated data products, metric definitions, and consumption experiences that turn engineered data into decisions.
This is not a traditional reporting leadership role; the classic notion of “reporting” in the form of a myriad of dashboards and filters is racing towards obsolescence. But the need for data and insights, and the need to deliver it in a way that is digestible and actionable, is timeless. Yes, governed dashboards and trusted reporting remain the foundation, and this leader must be excellent at that foundation. But the mandate is to move the organization decisively beyond static reporting toward a proactive, intelligent analytics capability: partnering with Data Science to productize and visualize their models, enabling generative AI and LLM-based access to our data, building exception-based systems that alert users when outcomes deviate from expectation in a statistically meaningful way, and designing agents that monitor data continuously and deliver insight without being asked.
Analytics engineering shares much of its DNA with data engineering — modeling, transformation, testing, version control, CI/CD, performance and cost discipline — but is oriented toward business enablement rather than platform and pipeline. Success in this role therefore depends as much on partnership as on technical depth. This leader will work shoulder to shoulder with Data Engineering on the boundary between platform and consumption, with Product Management on roadmap and requirements, with Data Science on advanced analytic products, and with Analytics Operations on a disciplined intake and prioritization process that makes the best possible use of finite capacity.
The ideal candidate has spent years building the traditional foundations — governance, metadata, lineage, dimensional modeling, engaging with enterprise BI platforms— and is now looking to apply that rigor to a fundamentally different generation of analytic products in new and innovative ways.
**What you'll be doing:**
**Organizational Leadership**
* Lead, coach, and develop an organization of approximately 30 people, including managing through frontline managers; own hiring, role clarity, career pathing, performance management, and succession planning.
* Define a multi-year vision and roadmap for enterprise reporting and analytics engineering, and translate it into quarterly outcomes the team and its partners can measure. Partner closely with Product Management to jointly shape the multi-year enterprise end-to-end data strategy.
* Own the organization's budget, vendor relationships, and contractor or offshore capacity.
* Establish and sustain an engineering culture within an analytics function: peer review, automated testing, documentation standards, source control, CI/CD, etc.
**Analytics Engineering and Data Architecture**
* Drive maturity of the last-mile architecture in partnership with Data Engineering: curated marts, semantic layers, reusable data products, and certified datasets that serve reporting, ai enablement, data science, and downstream applications.
* Define and enforce dimensional modeling standards, transformation frameworks, and modular, tested, version-controlled analytics code.
* Own the enterprise metric layer so that key business measures carry a single, governed definition regardless of where they are consumed.
* Partner with Data Engineering to define clear contracts and handoffs between pipeline and platform work and last-mile modeling, including shared tooling, standards, and escalation paths.
* Manage query performance, warehouse consumption, and platform cost as first-class engineering concerns.
**Data Governance, Metadata, and Lineage**
* Own cataloging, business glossary, data certification, and stewardship workflows, leveraging tools such as Atlan as the primary metadata platform.
* Maintain column-level lineage across the analytics estate to support impact analysis, change management, audit, and root-cause investigation.
* Leverage data access provisioning and entitlement models, including row- and column-level security, in partnership with Security, Privacy, and Compliance.
* Collaborate with Data Engineering to drive data quality monitoring, freshness and availability SLAs, observability, and incident response for analytic assets.
**Enterprise Reporting and Data Visualization**
* Drive analytics engagement by leveraging enterprise visualization and provisioning platforms, including Domo and Tableau, in partnership with Data Engineering. Ensure best practices are followed in data architecture, governance, adoption, performance, and total cost management.
* Set visualization and information design standards that make reports readable, consistent, accessible, and decision-oriented.
* Rationalize the existing reporting portfolio: retire redundant and unused assets, consolidate overlapping content, drive down tech debt and drive consumption toward certified sources.
* Build a durable self-service capability through training, templates, community, office hours, and clear guardrails on what belongs in self-service versus centrally managed content.
**Advanced, Proactive, and AI-Enabled Analytics**
* Partner with Data Science to productize their work: build the visualization, interaction, monitoring, and feedback loops that turn models and research into products the business actually uses.
* Partner with Product Management and Data Engineering to enable generative AI and LLM access to enterprise data. This includes preparing the semantic and metadata foundation that makes data legible to models, delivering conversational analytics, text-to-SQL, and retrieval-augmented experiences on governed sources, and establishing guardrails, evaluation, and accuracy monitoring so that answers can be trusted.
* Build exception-based analytics that detect when an outcome deviates from its expected value in a statistically significant way, using seasonality-aware baselines, forecast residuals, control limits, and anomaly detection rather than static thresholds.
* Route those exceptions to accountable owners with context, likely drivers, and a recommended next action; actively tune sensitivity and volume to prevent alert fatigue and preserve signal.
* Design and deploy analytic agents that proactively monitor data, investigate variances, assemble narrative explanations, and deliver insight into the tools where people already work.
* Shift the organization's consumption model from pull to push: the measure of success is not how many people opened a dashboard, but whether the right person was told the right thing at the right time.
**Cross-Functional Partnership, Intake, and Prioritization**
* Operate as a true partner to Product Management: contribute to roadmap, requirements, user research, and release planning, and run analytics with a product mindset covering personas, adoption metrics, and asset lifecycle management.
* Partner with Analytics Operations to run a transparent intake, triage, sizing, and prioritization process, with published capacity, explicit tradeoffs, and reliable delivery commitments.
* Make capacity constraints visible to stakeholders and executives, drive reuse over one-off builds, and decline or defer work with evidence rather than friction.
* Serve as a senior, executive-facing partner to business functions, translating ambiguous business questions into well-scoped analytic solutions.

* 15+ years of progressive experience in data, analytics, or business intelligence, including 8+ years leading teams and 4+ years managing managers.

* Experience applying software engineering practices to analytics work, including Git-based workflows, automated testing, and CI/CD.
* Enterprise-scale leveraging of BI and data visualization platforms such as Domo, Tableau, Power BI, or Looker, including governance, provisioning, adoption, and cost management.

job_title: Software Engineer, Platform - Reading, United Kingdom Reading, United Kingdom
job_description:
The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
Over 50 million people use Speechify’s text-to-speech products to turn whatever they’re reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify’s text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its 2025 Design Award winner for Inclusivity.
Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office.
**Overview**
The Platform team owns the backend behind everything Speechify ships: the public TTS API, payments, subscriptions, auth, consumption tracking, and analytics — serving over 50 million users across iOS, Android, Mac, Chrome, and web.
These are systems where correctness compounds. Subscription state has to stay consistent across five clients and two app-store billing systems that each go quiet at the worst moment. Consumption metering has to be exact enough to bill on and cheap enough to run at our request volume. The public TTS API has external customers with their own products depending on our latency and uptime. None of this degrades gracefully — it is either right, or someone gets charged twice.
The job is to make your own job smaller. Every system you own here should need less of you a year from now than it did the day you took it, and the reward for that is a larger one. That is the entire growth path on this team — there is no separate ladder, and no ceiling except the one you stop raising. We are a flat organization: people become leaders here by taking scope and being right about it, fast.
**What Yo****u’****ll Do**
* Design, build, and own the APIs behind payments, subscriptions, auth, consumption tracking, and our public TTS API
* Take on services you didn't write and make them faster, cheaper, and harder to break
* Establish that a change is correct before it ships, and leave behind the checks that keep it correct after you've moved on
* Automate the parts of your role that shouldn't need a person, then go take on what that freed you up for
* Turn work you've done once into work the whole team can repeat
* Design B2B and enterprise integrations for customers building on top of us
* Work with product, mobile, and web to keep backend architecture ahead of where the product is going
**An Ideal Candidate Should Have**
* Proven backend experience in TS/Node (required)
* Direct experience with GCP; working knowledge of AWS, Azure, or another cloud
* A habit of giving away work you used to own, and something to show for the room it created
* A daily working setup with AI agents you can describe in detail — what runs unattended, what you review, and where you've decided it doesn't get to act alone
* The instinct to check a result against the system itself — logs, database state, the actual request — rather than against a summary of it
* Judgment about what not to build, and the ability to say plainly why you dropped it
* A preference for being corrected over being right
* Preferred: Docker and containerized deployments
* Preferred: deploying high-availability applications on Kubernetes
**Interview process**
Several technical interviews plus a take-home assessment on a real codebase. We aim to finish within a week.
The assessment runs in two stages: you'll submit, get real feedback from an engineer on this team, and have time to act on it. Use the tools you use every day. You'll be asked to walk through your reasoning, so bring it.
**What We Offer**
* A dynamic environment where your contributions shape the company and its products
* A team that values innovation, intuition, and drive
* Autonomy, fostering focus and creativity
* The opportunity to have a significant impact in a revolutionary industry
* Competitive compensation, a welcoming atmosphere, and a commitment to an exceptional asynchronous work culture
* The privilege of working on a product that changes lives, particularly for those with learning differences like dyslexia, ADD, and more
* An active role at the intersection of artificial intelligence and audio – a rapidly evolving tech domain

Spendesk is the AI-powered spend management and procurement platform trusted by thousands of finance teams across Europe. * Own your area's economics — cost-to-serve, infra efficiency, hiring ROI — with a clear quarterly view, and present the commercial rationale behind your investment decisions.

* Be accountable for delivery and outcomes across your full portfolio of squads, balancing competing priorities without losing sight of quality.
* Establish group-level KPIs, SLOs, and operating rhythms so your teams run well without you in every room.

* Hire, develop, and retain a strong, balanced leadership team of EMs, Senior EMs, and Staff Engineers.
* Coach your managers through their hardest calls: performance conversations, hiring decisions, prioritisation trade-offs.

* Build succession plans for your key leadership roles, so no single departure puts your group at risk.

## The Role & Key Responsibilities
From your first day with us you will be part of a policing family making a real difference. It is our mission to identify and protect vulnerable people, prevent and respond to harm and keep people safe.
This role involves working within a centralised team, accepting referrals from divisional staff across the Force, in order to progress cases deemed suitable for an Out of Court Resolution (OoCR).
The OoCR Case Worker will be responsible for working through targeted interventions with adult offenders as part of an agreement, leading to an Out of Court Resolution as an alternative to being charged and having to attend court. This will be as part of a centralised team set up to reduce the demand on frontline officers, and provide a consistently high standard of interventions.
Key Accountabilities:
1. To contact victims of crime and ascertain what they need to ‘make it right’. To maintain and promote victim welfare and satisfaction as part of the conditional caution process, adhering to the victim’s code.
2. To contact offenders and carry out a needs assessment for adults to identify the reasons for offending.
3. To work with offenders with complex needs and be able to identify complex needs such as drug, drink addiction, and mental health issues.
4. To identify and use local interventions, with confidence to tailor agreements where appropriate, including community reparation opportunities.
5. To liaise with the Restorative Justice Team for conditional cautions following RJ principles, such as reparation activity.
6. To identify matters of a safeguarding nature involving any vulnerable adults and children identified during investigations and make appropriate referrals as necessary.
7. To establish and maintain good working relationships with appropriate local partners and colleagues within the organisation.

As a Support Worker, you will play a vital role within a multidisciplinary team (MDT) dedicated to helping individuals regain independence and achieve their rehabilitation goals.
Your work will focus on providing therapy-based support in community environments, empowering clients to improve their functional abilities and quality of life. As well as working along side the community nursing team to provide treatment for patients within their own homes.
We are seeking candidates who are compassionate and patient with a strong desire to support others. Good communication and interpersonal skills are essential, with the ability to work independently (including lone working) and as part of the wider MDT team.

* Support patients in developing and practicing skills needed for daily living and independence.
* Assist patients in setting realistic goals and motivate them to work towards achieving these objectives.
* Monitor and record patients' progress, using programmes such as EMIS, as well as providing feedback to the MDT and lead health care professional.
* Promote a safe and supportive environment, encouraging patients' confidence and participation.
* Collaborate with other team members, including physiotherapists, occupational therapists, and nurses, to ensure holistic care.
* Encourage and facilitate community engagement and participation for patients.

This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of Speech and Language Therapy across Essex. Joining NHS Essex ICB offers the chance to influence change at scale across a whole health and care system, working with 3 local authorities, education providers, universities and NHS and Local Authority commissioned providers. This role provides exceptional professional development, with opportunities to further develop advanced practice, strategic leadership, system transformation, education and research skills across the four pillars of advanced practice. You will work alongside senior leaders across health, education and social care, gaining unique experience in population health, workforce transformation and service improvement. If you are looking to make a lasting impact while progressing your career in an innovative, collaborative and forward-thinking organisation, this is an exciting opportunity to help shape the future for children and young people across Essex.

**Please note this role will only be offered as a secondment**

Provide strategic, population-level clinical leadership to improve outcomes for children and young people (0-25) with speech, language and communication needs.
Strengthen the Speech and Language Therapy (SLT) workforce through placements, apprenticeships, supervision and workforce development.
Increase access to SLT expertise in mainstream education and promote inclusive practice.
Work across health, education, local authority and SEND partnerships to support reform and system improvement.

## Job description
### Job responsibilities
**ROLE PURPOSE / SUMMARY**
The Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB) is a new organisation formed through the consolidation of three ICB areas in response to the NHSs ambition to deliver a more streamlined, strategic and cost-effective model of health commissioning. The ICB will oversee the commissioning of care for the approximately 2 million people who live in Essex. Operating within a reduced running cost envelope and aligned to the new requirements of ICBs in England, the ICB will focus on improving population health outcomes, health equity and smarter resource allocation.
The Speech and Language Therapy (SLT) Advanced Practitioner is a strategic, population-level clinical leadership role working across education, health and care systems to improve outcomes for children and young people aged 0-25 with speech, language and communication needs (SLCN).
The role will provide advanced clinical leadership across the Essex SEND partnership, working collaboratively with local authorities, Integrated Care Boards, NHS providers, education settings, universities, parent carer forums and professional networks to strengthen the Speech and Language Therapy workforce and increase access to SLT expertise within mainstream education settings. The post is aligned to the NHSE Multi-Professional Framework for Advanced Practice and operates across the four pillars of advanced practice: clinical practice, leadership and management, education, and research.
The post holder will:
* Provide strategic, population-level clinical SLT leadership to improve outcomes for children and young people (0-25) with speech, language and communication needs.
* Strengthen the SLT workforce pipeline across education settings through placements, apprenticeships and supervision capacity.
* Increase access to Speech and Language Therapy expertise within mainstream education settings.
* Support delivery of SEND reform and the Experts at Hand programme across the Essex system.

* Develop sustainable partnerships with Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), providers and wider stakeholders to strengthen workforce supply, capability and sustainability.
This is a strategic system leadership role and is not intended to carry a clinical caseload or undertake individual casework.

**Policy and service development**
* Lead the development and implementation of strategic initiatives that strengthen the Speech and Language Therapy workforce across mainstream education settings.
* Support implementation of national SEND reforms and the Experts at Hand programme across Essex.
* Influence policy development relating to workforce planning, education placements, apprenticeship pathways and inclusive practice.
* Ensure compliance with relevant NHS, HCPC, SEND and ICB governance requirements.
* Promote evidence-based practice and innovation across education, health and social care systems.

* Develop reports, business cases and recommendations for commissioners and system leaders.

* Contribute to delivery of relevant ICB and SEND partnership priorities.

* Contribute to business cases and investment proposals relating to workforce development initiatives.

* Ensure value for money and achievement of agreed programme outcomes.

* Support development of innovative placement supervision models.
* Build workforce capability through professional learning and development initiatives.
* Promote and support Speech and Language Therapy degree apprenticeships.

As the ICB continues to evolve, portfolios may be subject to change to reflect the needs of the organization, the health and care system and national policy direction. This may include adjustments to areas of responsibility or realignment of reporting structures.

## Overview
TBG Solutions designs and manufactures bespoke automated electrical test equipment for customers operating in demanding engineering sectors, including aerospace and defence.
We are looking for a Production Engineer to provide day-to-day technical support to our Cable Assembly team.
This is a practical engineering role focused on solving the problems that arise when bespoke cable and harness designs move from engineering documentation into manufacture. You will work closely with our Cable Assembly Engineers, Electrical Design Engineers, Production Manager, Quality team, Project teams, customers and suppliers to investigate build issues, resolve technical queries, address tooling problems and improve the information and processes used to manufacture our cable assemblies. Where a build cannot fully meet the released design, you may also be responsible for documenting the issue and supporting or obtaining formal customer concession approval before work proceeds.
Because much of our work is low-volume and project-specific, you will not simply be maintaining an established production line. You will regularly encounter new assemblies, new components and engineering challenges that require practical judgement and problem solving.
**About TBG Solutions**
TBG Solutions designs and manufactures bespoke automated test and measurement systems. Our projects bring together electrical, electronic, mechanical, software and systems engineering with in-house manufacturing and assembly.
Our Cable Assembly team manufactures the bespoke harnesses and interconnection assemblies used within our test systems, and this role will provide dedicated engineering support to that operation.
**Security**

Production Engineer – Cable Assembly

### Experience Required
**What we're looking for**
This role would particularly suit someone with a practical electrical manufacturing background who has progressed into production, manufacturing or engineering support.
**Essential**
* Practical experience with cable assemblies, wiring looms, harnesses, control panels or similar electrical manufacturing.
* Ability to read and understand electrical drawings, wiring diagrams and cable schedules.
* Good understanding of connectors, contacts, wire types, cable, sleeving, identification and termination methods.
* Understanding of crimping, soldering and other common cable assembly techniques.
* Experience troubleshooting manufacturing or assembly problems.
* Ability to document technical problems, proposed dispositions and supporting evidence clearly enough for internal approval and, where required, formal customer concession/deviation requests.
* Practical understanding of cable-assembly tooling and the ability to diagnose tooling, setup or process issues affecting build quality or repeatability.
* Ability to interpret BOMs and technical documentation.
* Good understanding of configuration and engineering change control.
* Ability to communicate effectively with Production and Design Engineering teams.
* Strong practical problem-solving skills.
* Comfortable working directly with manufacturing personnel on the shop floor.
* HNC/HND in Electrical, Electronic, Production or Manufacturing Engineering, or equivalent relevant experience.

* Low-volume, high-complexity manufacturing.
* Automated test equipment.

* Cable test equipment and continuity/insulation testing.

**The type of person who will suit the role**
We're looking for someone who enjoys solving practical engineering problems. You'll need to be comfortable moving between drawings, components and the actual assembly on the bench rather than working entirely from a desk.
You should be able to listen to the issue being raised by an experienced assembler, understand the underlying engineering problem and work collaboratively with Design Engineering to arrive at a practical solution.
Just as importantly, we want someone who asks why the problem occurred and how we prevent it happening again, rather than simply getting today's build moving. Where the correct resolution requires a design change, customer concession or new tooling, you should be comfortable driving that issue through to a properly documented and controlled outcome.

We believe in investing in our employees and supporting their career development through training, mentorship, and advancement opportunities. Join us and be part of a business that values diversity, equality, and inclusion, and is committed to delivering high-quality engineered solutions for our customers.
We’re always looking for new people to join us who represent our values. If you don’t see a role that complements your experience, you can always submit a speculative CV!
TBG Solutions are an equal opportunities employer.
### Responsibilities
**What you'll be doing**
Your main responsibility will be keeping cable assembly work progressing when technical or manufacturing issues arise.
* Provide hands-on technical support to Cable Assembly Engineers during manufacture.
* Investigate problems with drawings, wiring schedules, BOMs, connector details and assembly information.
* Resolve discrepancies between design documentation and the physical components being assembled.
* Work with Electrical Design Engineering to clarify or correct drawings and manufacturing information.
* Identify incorrect, unsuitable or difficult-to-manufacture design details and propose practical solutions.
* Support the introduction and manufacture of new cable and harness assemblies.
* Review cable designs for manufacturability before they reach Production.
* Support first-off builds and identify improvements before repeat manufacture.
* Produce and improve work instructions, build information and manufacturing documentation.
* Resolve production tooling issues and ensure the correct crimp tools, dies/locators, insertion and extraction tools, test fixtures and assembly aids are specified, available, suitable and maintained for the work being performed.
* Support component selection and identify suitable alternatives where parts become unavailable or unsuitable.
* Investigate production defects and non-conformances and help establish root cause and corrective action.
* Document deviations and non-conforming conditions clearly, prepare concession/deviation requests with appropriate technical evidence and rationale, and work with Quality, Engineering and Project teams to obtain and record customer approval where required.
* Feed manufacturing lessons back into the engineering team so recurring issues are designed out.
* Maintain accurate BOM and configuration information as designs change.
* Support Quality with inspection criteria and resolution of manufacturing queries.
* Work with suppliers where technical issues arise with connectors, cable, backshells, contacts or other bought-in components.
* Identify opportunities to improve quality, build time, repeatability and manufacturing efficiency.
**The sort of problems you'll solve**
The role is intended to be close to the people actually building the product. On a typical project you might be asked to investigate why:
* A backshell or connector cannot be assembled as shown on the drawing.
* The specified cable will not physically fit within the selected connector or gland.
* A crimp contact does not suit the specified wire gauge.
* A cable drawing, wiring schedule and BOM contain conflicting information.
* A component is obsolete or unavailable and an alternative is required.
* A harness cannot be routed or terminated as designed.
* A cable assembly is taking considerably longer to manufacture than expected.
* A recurring workmanship or quality issue needs its root cause identified.
* The specified tooling is unavailable, unsuitable, damaged, out of calibration or not producing a repeatable acceptable termination.
* The assembly cannot fully meet the released drawing or specification and the deviation needs to be technically assessed, documented and submitted to the customer for concession.
* The workshop needs clearer manufacturing or inspection instructions.
* A design technically works but is unnecessarily difficult to manufacture.
The expectation is not simply to report the problem back to Engineering. We want someone capable of understanding the issue, developing a sensible solution and working with the appropriate people to get it resolved.

We are not just a fintech company. We develop people by giving them the autonomy and the responsibility to challenge the status quo, so they can be the main actors of the change we want to bring to the market.
We are always looking for people better than us to join the team, disrupt payments, and revolutionise commerce in Europe. The goal we share, the mission is one, and at the end of the day we are just people trying to help other people.

Our sales agents are on the front lines, talking to merchants every day. Across the go to market systems they use to manage their sales, HubSpot CRM is where their deals, activities, conversations, reporting, automations and portfolio lives. When HubSpot works, our salespeople sell. When it breaks quietly in the background, deals stall, data drifts, and the people who trust the numbers stop trusting the tool.
**Your mission is to be the guardian of that system.** You are the person who keeps HubSpot healthy, honest, and trustworthy, so that every seller and every leader can rely on it without ever thinking about it.
This is not a caretaking job where you wait for tickets and tick them off. You are a detective and a builder. You go looking for what is wrong before anyone reports it, you find the real reason something failed instead of patching the symptom, and you make sure the same failure never happens twice. You turn a messy, growing CRM into a system people can trust, and you can prove it with data.
## **As the guardian of our CRM you will**
**Investigate root causes, not symptoms.** When something in HubSpot fails, you own it. You dig into what actually went wrong, validate the real root cause, and drive it to a fix. You are the single point of contact when the CRM misbehaves, and nothing gets dropped on your watch.
**Prevent the next bug before it happens.** You do not just close errors, you learn from them. You spot the patterns, harden the implementations that keep breaking, and put guardrails in place so a whole class of problems disappears. Every automation and implementation, local or global, follows our guidelines because you make sure it does, before and after it goes live.
**Measure the health of the CRM.** You build the dashboards that show, at a glance, whether what we ship actually works and keeps working. You track error rates, adoption, and data quality over time, so CRM health stops being a feeling and becomes a number we can watch and improve.
**Turn data into action.** You are as comfortable reading the numbers as fixing the system. You globalise and clean up our reporting once the requirements from Commercial Excellence are aligned, retire the dashboards no one needs, and use data to find the problems no one has noticed yet.
**Build and improve, hands on.** You create new automations and refine the ones we have, you read the logic of a workflow well enough to debug it, and you keep the instance clean, governed, and scalable across every market in Europe.
Your goal is to maximise the value and the trust in the CRM our salespeople rely on. Your success is measured in the health of the platform: fewer recurring failures, faster time to a real fix, cleaner data, and leaders who believe the numbers again because someone is watching them every day.
## **What is your story?**
You need to be eager to learn and improve every day. Some qualities you must have:
* A detective's instinct: you are not satisfied with a symptom, you want the root cause, and you enjoy the hunt
* An owner's mindset: you do not wait to be told, you know the instance and you act on it
* Reactive when it counts and proactive by default: when something breaks you are on it and you meet the SLA, and when you see a risk you raise it before it spreads
* Data-driven and analytical: you read data, understand the problem, and propose the fix
* The confidence to challenge a request rather than just take it, because requests will not only come from us, and the right thing to build is your job to protect
* Experience with a CRM (HubSpot ideal, Salesforce or similar is welcome), with ticketing and SLAs, and comfort building automations and reading the logic behind them
This is not a deep-specialist or heavy-code role. Understanding custom code is a plus, but the heart of the job is investigation, prevention, reporting, and governance. If you get satisfaction from taking something messy and making it trustworthy, this is your role.

**Job Title:** Workstream Project Manager – Architecture & Technology & Solution **Division:** Group **Remote**
**Purpose of Role**
The Workstream Project Manager – Architecture & Technology & Solution is accountable for driving day-to-day delivery execution across the S4+ Architecture, Technology and Solution workstreams, ensuring that architecture decisions, technical delivery, solution design, platform readiness and cross-stream technology dependencies are planned, coordinated, tracked and delivered in line with the integrated programme plan.
This role supports delivery of the S4+ target architecture and solution backbone across SAP S/4HANA core, surrounding SAP solutions, non-SAP platforms, integration, environments, data, security, tooling, testing, cutover and transition to support. The S4+ programme will implement a single SAP S/4 system across Minerals, ESCO and Corporate, with a target of 90% standardisation across core business processes and alignment to SAP fit-to-standard best practice.
The role works closely with the Chief Architect, S4+ Tech Lead, Integration Lead, Tooling SME, Product Domain Architects, Deloitte, SAP, PMO, Data, Security, Testing and Change teams to ensure solution and technology delivery remains aligned, governed and on plan.
The role is critical to ensuring S4+ delivers a harmonised, operable and future-ready technology platform that supports Weir’s Product Operating Model and Global Product Domains. Global Product Domains provide ownership of global processes, the data that underpins those processes, and the platforms and systems that enable them
**Objectives & Measurement - Key Responsibilities**
**Workstream Delivery & Execution**
* Drive day-to-day delivery across the Architecture, Technology and Solution workstreams, ensuring activity progresses in line with the integrated programme plan.
* Maintain detailed workstream plans covering architecture, technical delivery, solution design, integration, tooling, environments, security, testing, cutover and hypercare readiness.
* Track workstream milestones, deliverables, dependencies, risks, issues, assumptions and decisions.
* Ensure clear ownership of deliverables across Weir, Deloitte, SAP and third-party delivery teams.
* Coordinate delivery activity across architecture forums, technical working groups, design authority meetings and programme governance.
* Identify delivery slippage early and work with accountable leads to define corrective action or recovery plans.
* Ensure Architecture, Technology and Solution workstream outputs are delivered within agreed scope, time, quality and budget parameters.
**Architecture & Solution Governance**
* Support the Chief Architect and S4+ Tech Lead in coordinating architecture and solution governance across the programme.
* Track design decisions, architecture actions, open risks, technical assumptions and escalation items through the appropriate governance forums.
* Support preparation of materials for the Design Authority, Technical Working Group and related architecture governance meetings.
* Ensure decisions are documented, owned, followed up and reflected in workstream plans.
* Help ensure solution decisions align with enterprise architecture, Clean Core principles, fit-to-standard guidance and future operating model requirements.
* Track exceptions, divergences from standard, open design points and unresolved cross-domain decisions.
* Support escalation of material solution or architecture conflicts with clear options, impacts and recommendations.
**Technology Delivery Coordination**
* Coordinate planning and delivery activity across technology components including S/4HANA core, SAP RISE, cloud infrastructure, environments, landing zones, integration, security, data platforms and wider SAP/non-SAP ecosystem dependencies.
* Work with the S4+ Tech Lead to ensure technology delivery plans are aligned to SAP Activate phases and programme milestones.
* Track technology readiness for build, system integration testing, user acceptance testing, performance testing, cutover rehearsals, go-live and hypercare.
* Ensure technical dependencies are visible and actively managed across data, integration, security, environments, testing and operational readiness.
* Support delivery governance between Weir, Deloitte, SAP, hyperscaler and other technology partners.
* Help ensure the S4+ solution is designed and delivered for scalability, resilience, supportability and future AI / automation readiness. The Board Paper identifies scalable cloud infrastructure, AI readiness, harmonised data and real-time analytics as key elements of the S4+ scope and future value.
**Solution Design & Cross-Domain Alignment**
* Coordinate delivery activity across solution design workstreams, ensuring functional, technical, data and integration activities remain aligned.
* Support end-to-end solution planning across value streams and Product Domains.
* Track solution design dependencies across domains such as Finance, Sales, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Service, Engineering, Data and Procurement.
* Ensure open design issues are captured, prioritised and escalated through the right decision forums.
* Support alignment between business process design, solution architecture, technical delivery and future-state operating model.
* Help ensure design activity supports harmonised global value streams rather than re-creating local or divisional fragmentation.
* Reinforce the programme’s move away from fragmented, local or point-solution decision-making towards a single integrated global operating model aligned to SAP S/4HANA and future digital capabilities.
**Integrated Planning, Dependencies & RAID Management**
* Own detailed planning and dependency management for Architecture, Technology and Solution workstream activities.
* Maintain workstream plans and ensure they are aligned with the overall integrated programme plan.
* Identify and manage dependencies across architecture, functional domains, integration, data, security, testing, tooling, change, infrastructure and supplier teams.
* Maintain accurate RAID logs and ensure risks and issues have clear owners, mitigations, due dates and escalation routes.
* Track cross-workstream dependencies and ensure blockers are escalated early.
* Support PMO reporting with accurate, evidence-based status updates.
* Ensure programme leadership has clear visibility of critical technology and solution risks that may impact timeline, cost, quality or readiness.
**SAP Activate Gate & Delivery Readiness Support**
* Support SAP Activate-aligned planning and governance across Architecture, Technology and Solution workstreams.
* Track readiness against key phase gates, entry criteria and exit criteria.
* Ensure required evidence is collected and maintained for architecture, solution design, technical build, test readiness, deployment and hypercare.
* Support gate reviews by coordinating inputs from architecture, technology, integration, data, security, testing and partner teams.
* Identify gaps in readiness evidence and drive follow-up actions to closure.
* Help ensure workstream deliverables are audit-ready and aligned to programme governance expectations.
* Support the programme methodology, which combines SAP Activate alignment with agile ways of working and earlier system testing during design and build.
**Tooling, Reporting & Delivery Controls**
* Work with the Tooling SME and PMO to ensure Architecture, Technology and Solution workstream delivery is tracked in the agreed programme tools.
* Maintain accurate workstream reporting across plans, milestones, RAID, dependencies, decisions, actions and readiness status.
* Support the use of tools such as LeanIX, Signavio, SAP Cloud ALM, Tricentis, Jira, SharePoint and other programme repositories where relevant.
* Ensure delivery evidence, architecture artefacts, decision records and technical status updates are maintained consistently.
* Support traceability between architecture decisions, solution designs, backlog items, test evidence and delivery milestones.
* Provide clear and concise reporting for programme governance, workstream meetings and leadership updates.
* Help ensure reporting is focused on decisions required, delivery risks, blockers and forward-looking actions.

* Track partner deliverables, assumptions, dependencies, risks and actions across Architecture, Technology and Solution workstreams.

**Essential**

* Ability to challenge unclear ownership, delivery gaps, missed actions or unmanaged dependencies constructively.

What makes these clubs unique is that the coach weighs each player before their game. Players earn bonus goals for their weight loss so the league is decided not only on points won, but pounds lost.
The clubs have been hugely successful with players losing hundreds of thousands of lbs since the programme launched in January 2016 - this has led to the FA and Sport England endorsing our work and supporting the programme. We now have over 160 clubs across the UK!
Check out our appearance on BBC Breakfast here!
We’re looking for a dedicated MAN v FAT Club Referee to officiate games on a weekly basis at Havant RFC, Hooks Lane Ground, Fraser Road, Havant, **Monday, from 7 - 8pm).** The role would suit an individual who shares our passion for rugby and supporting men in making health and lifestyle improvements in order to lose weight. Excellent communication skills and an in depth knowledge of the laws of the game is essential.
Please note: MAN v FAT Rugby follow the Touch format; T1 MAN v FAT Rugby Rules
MAN v FAT Referees are human and valued members of our community. Respect the referee, the referee’s decision is final. No Ref, No Game.
The authority of the referee
Each game is controlled by a referee who has full authority to enforce the Laws of the Game in connection with the game to which they have been appointed, from the moment they enter the locality where the playing area is situated until they leave.
Powers and duties of the referee:
\* Enforces the Laws of the Game within the spirit of MAN v FAT Rugby.
\* Allows play to continue when the team against which an offence has been committed will benefit from such an advantage and penalises the original offence if the anticipated advantage does not ensue at that time.
\* Keeps a record of the match and provides the appropriate authorities with a game report which includes information on any disciplinary action taken against players, and/or team officials and any other incidents which occur before, during or after the game. Follow the incident report procedure to escalate any necessary misconduct and disciplinary action taken during the game. This should include keeping notes of any incidents they would like to report including language used, player names and actions. This will enable us to take appropriate action at a provider level and ensure referees are suitably supported.
\* Acts as timekeeper.
\* Stops, suspends or terminates the game for any infringement of the Laws or due to any kind of outside interference.
\* Takes disciplinary action against players guilty of cautionable and sending-off offences.
\* Ensures that no unauthorised persons enter the playing area.
\* Stops the game if, in their opinion, upon injury assessment a player is seriously injured and ensures that he is removed from the playing area. Ensuring any player bleeding from a wound leaves the playing area. Allows play to continue until there is a stoppage in play if a player is, in their opinion, only slightly injured
\* Ensures that any ball used meets the requirements and players are wearing the correct equipment.
\* Make use of timed suspensions to exclude temporarily players guilty of infringements of the laws. The referee should make excluded players aware of the end of their period of suspension.
\* Report match scores to the club coach at the end of the session

What makes these clubs unique is that the coach weighs each player before their game. Players earn bonus goals for their weight loss so the league is decided not only on points won, but pounds lost.
The clubs have been hugely successful with players losing hundreds of thousands of lbs since the programme launched in January 2016 - this has led to the FA and Sport England endorsing our work and supporting the programme. We now have over 160 clubs across the UK!
Check out our appearance on BBC Breakfast here!
We’re looking for a dedicated MAN v FAT Club Referee to officiate games on a weekly basis at **Alderwood Leisure Centre, Tongham Rd, Aldershot****, Friday from 7 - 8pm).** The role would suit an individual who shares our passion for rugby and supporting men in making health and lifestyle improvements in order to lose weight. Please note: MAN v FAT Rugby follow the Touch format; T1 MAN v FAT Rugby Rules
MAN v FAT Referees are human and valued members of our community. Respect the referee, the referee’s decision is final. No Ref, No Game.
The authority of the referee
Each game is controlled by a referee who has full authority to enforce the Laws of the Game in connection with the game to which they have been appointed, from the moment they enter the locality where the playing area is situated until they leave.
Powers and duties of the referee:
\* Enforces the Laws of the Game within the spirit of MAN v FAT Rugby.
\* Allows play to continue when the team against which an offence has been committed will benefit from such an advantage and penalises the original offence if the anticipated advantage does not ensue at that time.
\* Keeps a record of the match and provides the appropriate authorities with a game report which includes information on any disciplinary action taken against players, and/or team officials and any other incidents which occur before, during or after the game. Follow the incident report procedure to escalate any necessary misconduct and disciplinary action taken during the game. This should include keeping notes of any incidents they would like to report including language used, player names and actions. This will enable us to take appropriate action at a provider level and ensure referees are suitably supported.
\* Acts as timekeeper.
\* Stops, suspends or terminates the game for any infringement of the Laws or due to any kind of outside interference.
\* Takes disciplinary action against players guilty of cautionable and sending-off offences.
\* Ensures that no unauthorised persons enter the playing area.
\* Stops the game if, in their opinion, upon injury assessment a player is seriously injured and ensures that he is removed from the playing area. \* Ensures that any ball used meets the requirements and players are wearing the correct equipment.

About Tripadvisor
The Tripadvisor Group connects people to experiences worth sharing, and aims to be the world’s most trusted source for travel and experiences. We leverage our brands, technology, and capabilities to connect our global audience with partners through rich content, travel guidance, and two-sided marketplaces for experiences, accommodations, restaurants, and other travel categories. The subsidiaries of Tripadvisor, Inc. (Nasdaq: TRIP), include a portfolio of travel brands and businesses, including Tripadvisor, Viator, and TheFork.
At Tripadvisor experiences, the only thing we love more than travel is data. We slice it, we dice it, and we use it to empower our decision making.
What You will do:
As a Data Scientist on our experimentation team you will work with product teams across Viator to measure whether the changes they ship actually worked, defining the metrics that matter and making sure the decisions that follow are sound.
Part of your contribution is making experimentation easier for the teams you support, through reusable tooling, clear documentation and consistent practice. Viator sells experiences that travellers often book once a year, in a marketplace where supply is finite and shared, so you will be learning to navigate problems where the obvious analysis can give the wrong answer, with support from senior practitioners who have done it before.
You will:
Design and analyse experiments end to end with the product teams you support, working directly with the Product Managers and Engineers who will act on the results.
Turn product questions into testable hypotheses with pre-registered primary metrics, appropriate guardrails, and an honest view of what the available traffic can and cannot detect before the experiment starts.
Define and instrument feature-level metrics, understanding how metric choice affects sensitivity, interpretation and the decision a team is trying to make.
Investigate results properly, checking assignment integrity, exposure and data quality before conclusions are drawn, and treating a surprising result as something to diagnose rather than announce.
Build reusable queries, tooling and templates and apply our shared protocols, so teams can run good experiments faster and with less rework.
Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including inconclusive and negative results, with a recommendation attached rather than a table of numbers.
Look beyond whether a change worked to why it worked, and flag when a result may not hold for other users, markets or time periods.
Carry out analysis beyond experiments, including opportunity sizing, funnel and behavioural analysis, and observational measurement where randomisation isn't possible.
Document hypotheses, designs, outcomes and decisions so results remain comparable and the organisation compounds what it learns.
Grow your own depth in experimentation and causal inference, with review and mentorship from senior and principal data scientists.
Skills & Experience
Experience: Solid experience in data science or a similar quantitative role, supporting and influencing product teams.
Statistical & Experimentation Foundations: Sound understanding of experimentation beyond running it through a platform, including statistical power and minimum detectable effect, the difference between an inconclusive result and no effect, why peeking and post-hoc metric selection cause problems, and the common ways an experiment can be invalid.
Technical & Modelling Expertise: Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, with hands-on experience of statistical analysis and experimentation, and some exposure to statistical modelling or machine learning techniques such as regression and classification.
Product Acumen: Ability to define, implement and operationalise product and feature-level metrics, with support from senior colleagues on the most complex cases.
Partnership: Experience working closely with Product Managers and Engineers as a trusted partner, and a willingness to make things easier for those teams through tooling, documentation and consistent practice.
Critical Thinking: A habit of asking whether a result is trustworthy before asking what it means, and comfort saying so when it isn't.
Communication: Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain statistical reasoning to people without a statistical background and to hold your position constructively when a result is unwelcome.
Education: Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Engineering, Physics, Economics, or a related quantitative field.
You could be an especially great fit if you have:
Experience with metrics that are difficult to measure, such as sparse conversion, heavy-tailed revenue, or slow-to-observe outcomes.
Familiarity with variance reduction techniques and why they matter for sensitivity.
Exposure to causal inference methods for situations where randomisation isn't available.
Experience with SaaS experimentation tools such as Statsig, Eppo or GrowthBook, or with an in-house platform.
Experience in a high-scale consumer product environment such as a marketplace, e-commerce or travel platform.
An interest in how modern AI tooling can make analysis faster and experimentation more accessible to product teams.

Join Tripledot Studios as a Senior Machine Learning Engineer working on dynamic pricing and recommender systems use cases in our games. You'll focus on understanding the data, developing features and improving the models, rather than primarily owning production deployment.
You'll work toward defined near-term ML targetds, collaborating with the monetization team and game product teams to plan A/B tests. Over the longer term, you'll work with those teams to translate product and monetization requirements into ML objectives.

* Build and improve training pipelines for dynamic pricing and recommender system models, from feature and label design through training, tuning and offline evaluation of tabular models such as neural networks and gradient-boosted trees.

* As you get up to speed, identify gaps in the team's understanding of the models and propose improvements to their direction.

* Experience designing features and labels, choosing metrics for the decision a model makes and judging when offline results warrant an A/B test.

The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.

## **Your mission**
UiPath’s Intelligence Document Processing drives understanding of the documents and messages on which a business runs: invoices, claims, contracts, customer emails. We use frontier LLMs to turn all of that into structured data that automations and AI agents can act on. You'll be building the product that does it: the ingestion and extraction pipelines, the APIs customers build their operations on top of, and the systems that make those models useful, fast and trustworthy at enterprise scale.
Increasingly that work is agentic. What you build is what lets AI agents ingest, understand, retrieve and reason over enterprise documents at volume, without giving up accuracy, security or governance.
It's a product engineering role with complex systems and LLM-in-production problems underneath it. The same service handles a customer's first ten documents and another's ten million, runs in our cloud and inside a bank's own air-gapped datacentre, and has to be good enough that a business will act on its output. Knowing how well the models are actually doing, and what to do when the answer is "not well enough", is a large part of the job.
You'll write in several languages here, and pick up new ones as the problem demands. We care much more about how you think than about what you've written it in. We're looking for someone who loves building things, learns fast, and wants to own product outcomes rather than tickets.
## **What you'll do at UiPath**
* Work with engineers, product managers and customers to design, build and operate the AI systems behind UiPath's document processing products.
* Build across the pipeline: ingestion, parsing and extraction, indexing and retrieval, and the evaluation that tells us any of it is working.
* Take features from idea to production and stay with them, measuring whether they actually worked, and improving them when they didn't.
* Solve genuinely hard problems in concurrency, latency and distributed systems, so the platform holds up under high-volume production workloads.
* Build for environments we don't control: multi-cloud, on-premises, air-gapped, and under strict security and compliance requirements.
* Use coding agents as a serious part of your toolkit, and help the team get better at it. Where to trust them, where not to, and how to keep quality high as the tooling changes underneath us.
* Work with teams across UiPath and across locations to innovate and build best-in-class document processing, and occasionally with customers directly. Because the fastest way to understand a product is to watch someone use it.
* Contribute to our engineering culture: mentor, review, hire, and push back when something isn't good enough.
## **What you'll bring to the team**
* A solid track record (5+ years) building and operating large-scale commercial services that real customers depend on.
* Strong programming ability and the confidence to pick up whatever language a problem calls for. You'll meet Python, Rust and C# here, but we don't expect you to arrive knowing them all.
* Real-world experience with cloud platforms (Azure, AWS or GCP) and containerised deployment on Kubernetes. You understand how production systems get shipped, monitored and scaled, not just written.
* Comfort with data at scale: SQL, and the trade-offs between different storage and search systems.
* Experience working with coding agents, and opinions about them, What responsible use looks like, where they earn their keep and where they cost you, and how you keep evaluating them in an ecosystem that changes every few months.
* An appreciation for tools that catch bugs before runtime — type systems, tests, and designs that make bad states unrepresentable. Especially in the age of coding agents.
* A pragmatic grasp of computer science fundamentals. We care about solving real problems with the right data structure, not reciting one from a textbook.
* Experience shipping LLM-backed products to production is a strong plus: prompting, evaluation, and everything else that turns a model into a feature people will trust.
* Familiarity with document processing is a plus: OCR, layout, and the messy reality of documents as they actually arrive.
* An opinion on what makes good code and good architecture, and the ability to argue it, including against us.
* You're a builder and a problem-solver at heart.

The Business Head for the Marlin product line is a senior commercial and technical leader responsible for the overall performance, growth, and strategic direction of the Marlin portfolio. Reporting to the VP Marine Business, this leader ensures strong revenue growth, market competitiveness, operational efficiency, and continuous innovation within the Marlin business.

The Marlin Business brings together commercial, product, software development and technical support capabilities to develop and grow innovative software and services for the marine industry.

* Conduct market analysis to identify new opportunities, customer needs, and emerging technology trends.
* Ensure alignment and collaboration with other business lines across Sercel Concept, Sercel and Viridien.

* Drive revenue growth, expand market presence, and strengthen customer relationships.
* Oversee pipeline management, pricing strategy, contract negotiations, and sales performance tracking.

* Prioritize features and investments based on market opportunity, ROI, and technical feasibility.
* Ensure strong lifecycle management from product design through release and ongoing enhancements.

* Ensure timely, reliable delivery of high-quality software releases.
* Promote agile development practices, engineering excellence, and continuous improvement.

### **A little bit about our team**
Sureel AI is building the standards and infrastructure for AI rights, licensing, attribution, protection, and intelligence, starting in music and expanding across media.
We are building the infrastructure that enables creators and rights holders to control how their work is used by AI, protect their rights, understand its use and value, and participate in new AI licensing models. We also provide AI companies and digital platforms with the systems they need to access rights, permissions, attribution, guardrails, reporting, and licensing infrastructure programmatically.
Acquired by Warner Music Group, Sureel operates as an independent, federated company, combining startup speed with the reach of a global music company.
Our commercial relationships sit at the heart of what we're building: with the AI companies and digital service providers (DSPs) who integrate our attribution infrastructure into their platforms, and with the rights holders whose works and interests that infrastructure protects. As Director, Business Development & Licensing, you'll own the business function across both sides of that equation, working closely with senior leadership, cross-functional teams, and external partners across the music, technology, and legal worlds. Your work will directly shape the commercial architecture of AI attribution at scale.
### **Your role**
You will lead Sureel's business function, reporting to the CEO and two Co-Presidents. This is a senior, commercially focused role. When Sureel is negotiating with a service provider or a rights holder, you will own the business function of that negotiation.
You will also serve as Sureel's primary liaison with industry bodies such as DDEX and regulatory bodies such as WIPO where their activities relate to Sureel's business.
A key part of the role will be developing business models and modeling outcomes for charging clients, including DSPs and AI companies. A strong understanding of economics and music rights will be important.
Your objective is to structure agreements that increase adoption of Sureel's infrastructure, create repeatable commercial models, and establish frameworks that can scale across multiple rights holders, AI companies, and markets.
You will negotiate licensing models, revenue structures, payment flows, and the economic frameworks that determine how permissions through Sureel's technology translate into compensation. You will also oversee the business use cases for integrating Sureel's infrastructure with AI companies and DSPs, defining what a commercially viable integration looks like and structuring the terms around it.
You'll work closely with Product and Client Relations. They will bring the product and partner perspectives, while you will lead the commercial structure and economics that support the business.
This is an opportunity to help define the business function of a company working in a new and evolving area, and to help shape how creators are compensated in the age of AI.
### What you'll do:
* **Own the business function for Sureel's negotiations**, whether with AI companies, DSPs, other digital service providers, or rights holders, leading commercial strategy, deal structure, and terms from first conversation through signature.
* **Negotiate the economics of platform integrations**, including licensing models, revenue structures, payment flows, and frameworks that reflect the value of Sureel's technology alongside rights holders' catalog and distribution positions.
* **Develop the business use cases for integrating Sureel's infrastructure** with AI companies and DSPs, defining commercial success and prioritizing opportunities based on enterprise value.
* **Develop licensing and economic frameworks for an emerging category**, using relevant AI and rights-technology transactions to inform agreements that can work across different partners and markets.
* **Structure multi-stakeholder commercial arrangements** among rights holders and industry participants, positioning Sureel's infrastructure as the mechanism for executing those agreements.
* **Partner with Client Relations on rights-holder relationships**, owning the commercial terms and deal economics while they lead the broader relationship and delivery.
* **Work closely with Warner Music Group counterparts** on commercial terms, licensing structures, and strategic priorities.
* **Provide market intelligence** on emerging technologies, competitive developments, licensing innovation, and deal dynamics across the AI and DSP landscape.
* **Represent Sureel with industry and standards organizations**, including DDEX, WIPO, and other initiatives shaping AI rights and licensing.
* **Develop pricing and packaging for Sureel's platform**, including enterprise fees, API and usage-based pricing, transaction fees, revenue share, licensing administration, analytics, and hybrid structures.
* **Create repeatable commercial and licensing frameworks** that can scale across partners rather than requiring every agreement to be built from scratch.
* **Help structure how Sureel infrastructure is used in commercial agreements**, including rights, permissions, guardrails, attribution, reporting, and economic obligations between rights holders and AI companies.
* **Handle confidential and proprietary information,** including deal terms, partner economics, and negotiations with discretion and integrity.
* **Help shape emerging industry standards and licensing frameworks** so they can be implemented programmatically and work with Sureel's architecture.
### Who you are:
* You have deep experience structuring and negotiating commercial agreements in **music, media, or technology**, including licensing deals, platform integrations, revenue-share structures, or rights-technology transactions.
* You've owned the business side of negotiations with platforms, DSPs, technology companies, or rights holders and carried complex deals from term sheet through signature.
* You understand the economics of the music industry: how rights generate revenue, how licensing frameworks are built, and how value flows between platforms, intermediaries, and rights holders.
* You're comfortable with data and financial detail. You can model a revenue structure, pressure-test assumptions, and explain the business logic clearly to technical teams and senior counterparties.
* You can structure complex deals and find approaches that work for the different parties involved.
* You build trust quickly and can represent leadership in high-stakes negotiations, make judgment calls on terms, and know when to escalate.
* You communicate clearly in writing and in person and can stay calm in a fast-moving environment.
* You understand how pricing, licensing structures, technical standards, and ecosystem incentives can support platform adoption and durable commercial outcomes.
* You are interested in the music industry and enjoy working in a small, collaborative, startup-paced team.
### We'd love it if you also had:
* Direct experience negotiating with AI companies, DSPs, or other digital service providers on licensing, integration, or commercial partnership terms.
* Experience working with artists, labels, publishers, or CMOs/PROs on the commercial side, or serving as a senior deal advisor to them.
* Experience across deal structuring and licensing, business development, commercial strategy, or partnerships.
* Involvement in industry licensing, standards, or policy initiatives shaping how AI and rights interact.
* Experience working directly with C-level executives on commercial strategy, negotiation preparation, and translating senior conversations into agreements.
* Experience developing commercial models for infrastructure, APIs, marketplaces, payments, rights technology, or other platforms where value is monetized across multiple layers of a transaction.
* Curiosity about the music and entertainment landscape and AI's impact on creators.

APPLY NOW
### Manage Cyber and QA accreditations across the defence sector
**Job Title: Group Senior Quality Engineer: Defence**
**Reporting to: Quality Compliance Manager**
**Location: Thatcham-UK or Milton Keynes-UK or Jois-Austria (Hybrid)**
Xtrac is the world’s leading design and manufacture of specialist transmissions. Our customers include the top motorsports racing series including Formula One, Le Mans, IndyCar and NASCAR and we also supply transmissions for the most exclusive high-performance cars in the world. We are at the forefront of a once-in-a-generation opportunity as the automotive industry transitions from internal combustion to electric and hybrid and our experienced and dedicated teams are using the latest cutting-edge technology to achieve this transition.
Xtrac also has a new partnership with Zoerkler, a specialist in gear manufacture and precision engineering. This strategic venture marks a significant step forward in our ambitious growth plans and reinforces our commitment to delivering world-class transmission components and systems to our customers.
**The Role**
The Group Senior Quality Engineer – Defence is accountable for qualifying our Portfolio Company (Xtrac+Helix+New Eagle+Zoerkler) as a supplier to UK MoD, NATO and US DoD programmes, so that no defence opportunity is lost for want of a certification. Reporting to the Group Quality Compliance Manager, the role begins with gap analysis against AQAP 2110 and JSP 940 across the sites to establish the true cost, timescale and options for positioning the business, and then champions those certification programmes through to approval across the applicable sites who are accountable for their delivery.
The role works alongside the site quality managers rather than a direct team and holds the group relationship with DE&S, DECA and the relevant national quality assurance authorities, works alongside the IT and Information Security Lead on the cyber accreditations that UK MoD and US DoD now treat as entry conditions, and supports Engineering on defence functional safety requirements. It works through the Group Central Quality Organisation and is the authority Commercial relies on before answering a quality clause in an MoD, US DoD or NATO tender.
**Day to Day**
**Essential Duties**
* Commission and manage AQAP 2110/ JSP 940 gap assessments across the sites, then advise and facilitate the certification programme through to approval — quality plans, deliverable evidence, risk management, government quality assurance interface and audit readiness.
* Produce a costed, resourced and prioritised view of what defence accreditation requires of the group, so that the business can decide where and when to invest and which opportunities it can credibly pursue.
* Own the working relationship with DE&S, DECA, NATO national quality assurance authorities and any Government Quality Assurance Representative.
* Maintain defence accreditation on a strictly site and geography-specific basis, ensuring no group-level consolidation mixes customer or national security data across the UK, US and Austrian entities.
* Support Facility Security Clearance and personnel vetting requirements with the Industrial Operations Director and advise the quality system and record-keeping side of export control.
* Support Engineering on related defence functional safety requirements, ensuring safety evidence on defence programmes is captured, authorised and retained.
* Act as the authority on MoD, DoD and NATO quality clauses in RFQ’s and contracts: what the group can commit to today, what it cannot, and what it takes to close the difference.
* Support customer audits and supplier qualification submissions.
* Support the sites in closing identified gaps by standardising defence-related processes, procedures and policies across the group.
* Responsible for preparing and facilitating external defence audits.
* Build internal auditor competence at the sites against the defence standards.
* Report defence accreditation status, gaps and contract-readiness flags monthly into the Quality Performance Pack and to the Quality & Accreditation Council, escalating slippage early rather than absorbing it.
Perform other duties as assigned.
**About You**
**Required Qualifications/ Experience**
* Demonstrable experience implementing, maintaining or being assessed against AQAP 2110 in a global defence supply chain.
* Working knowledge of JSP 940 and the UK MoD contractor assurance model, with direct dealings with DE&S, DECA or an appointed Government Quality Assurance Representative.
* Demonstrated ability to conduct structured gap analysis against a standard and translate the findings into a costed, resourced and credible closure plan.
* Experience operating across jurisdictions, and the judgement to keep defence evidence and data properly segregated between entities.
* Evidence of delivering change across multiple sites or legal entities without direct line authority, and of holding certification bodies and internal stakeholders to a committed date.
* Strong written communication skills, with the ability to author clear procedures, determinations and audit reports that will stand up to external assessment.
* Right to work in the UK or the EU, and willingness to travel routinely between the UK, Austria and the USA.
**Preferred Qualifications/ Experience**
* Wider AQAP familiarity, US supply chain, defence software and functional safety experience.
* AS9100 or EN 9100 experience alongside the defence standards.
* Current SC or DV clearance; membership of a recognised quality institute.
* Formal root cause and problem-solving qualification such as Six Sigma.
* Working level German, for the Jois site.
